jobs.title: Kitchen Helper (Part-Time)
jobs.description:
Part-time position - 10 Hours per week

Salary Range: $16.00 Hourly

Reports To:

The Kitchen Helper reports to the Culinary Services Director, Executive Chef, or other designated Culinary Services leader.

FLSA Classification:

This position is classified as non-exempt and is an hourly position.

Job Overview:

Supports the culinary team with dishwashing, sanitation, cleaning, and routine meal preparation and service-support tasks. Helps ensure the kitchen, dining service areas, and meal service operations are clean, organized, stocked, and prepared to provide excellent service to residents and guests.

Responsibilities and Duties:

• Maintain a safe, clean, and organized work environment in accordance with sanitation standard operating procedures.

• Operate dishwashing equipment safely and properly; wash, clean, and store pots, pans, cooking utensils, plates, glasses, cups, silverware, and other foodservice equipment.

• Maintain adequate cleaning supplies, monitor chemical dispensers, use required safety equipment, and remove kitchen trash and refuse as needed.

• Support preparation for meal service through simple kitchen tasks such as washing and preparing fruits and vegetables, placing prepared items into pans or service containers, assembling salads, plating desserts, portioning or arranging items for service, and assisting with tray setup.

• Assist servers with side work and routine setup tasks to ensure dining areas and service stations are prepared for each meal service.

• Assist with room service tray delivery and the delivery and retrieval of meal carts to and from satellite kitchens or designated service areas.

• Assist during meal service by removing soiled dishes from dining areas and returning them to the dishwashing station.

• Participate in required in-service training and follow all Federal, State, and local regulations, as well as community policies and procedures.

• Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

• High school diploma or GED preferred

• Prior food service, kitchen, or hospitality experience preferred

• Ability to follow written and verbal instructions

• Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment

Physical Abilities:

• While performing the duties of this job, the associate is often required to stand, walk, sit, use fine and gross motor skills, reach with hands and arms, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, talk, hear, and smell.  • An individual in this position will be required to lift or carry weight in up to 50 lbs. Intermittent physical activity includes lifting and supporting residents. The associate must use proper body mechanics.

Benefits Offered (for Part-Time Employees):

• Paid Time Off (PTO)
• Flexible Schedule
• On the job training
• Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
• Free Parking

Other Compensation Programs:

• Employee Referral Bonus
• Resident Referral Bonus

Equal Opportunity Statement:

Monarch Communities and Brandywine Senior Living is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

We comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Talent Analyst, Value Creation Team
jobs.description:
Overview

Help build the leadership teams and talent networks that drive growth across LLR’s portfolio companies. LLR’s Talent Analyst supports executive and board searches for LLR portfolio companies as part of the Human Capital group within the Value Creation Team. Working with search leads and portfolio stakeholders, you’ll turn market insight into strong candidate pipelines and keep each search moving. You’ll also drive value creation initiatives, including the portfolio job board (Getro), the portfolio executive roster and alumni network, and talent database pipelines. This role combines hands-on executive talent research and sourcing with ownership of portfolio-wide talent initiatives, offering exposure to both the people and business challenges of growing companies.

This is a hybrid role, and in-office expectations are set by the Human Capital team based on each search’s needs. A successful candidate thrives with strong self-management: you’ll set your own workplans, track milestones independently, and keep search leads and portfolio stakeholders informed through clear, timely communication, whether you’re in the office or working remotely.

Accountabilities

• Partner with search leads and portfolio company stakeholders at the start of each search to clarify role requirements, success profiles, and target organizations, then build a focused sourcing plan.

• Build and maintain market maps by researching target industries, companies, and talent; identify target organizations and candidates, build pipelines, and share concise findings that shape search priorities.

• Keep candidate records, notes, and status accurate and current in LLR's talent database, following confidentiality, privacy, and recordkeeping practices.

• Coordinate search materials, communications, and logistics; track milestones, keep stakeholders informed, and raise risks or changes early.

• Own project management for value creation initiatives across the portfolio, including portfolio job board management, portfolio organization health monitoring, and portfolio-wide executive talent roster monitoring: set workplans and milestones, coordinate stakeholders, and report on progress and outcomes.

Skills and Requirements

• Bachelor's degree.

• At least one year of experience in talent sourcing, recruiting, or executive search.

• Knowledge of sourcing and research methods, including Boolean searching, professional networks, and talent databases. LinkedIn Recruiter experience or comparable sourcing platforms required.

• Comfort with AI-enabled tools and modern recruiting technology; able to develop AI-driven approaches that improve research, outreach, and workflows, while verifying outputs and applying sound judgment.

• Strong research, analytical, and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to connect company and market context to candidate profiles and search priorities.

• Track record of managing multiple cross-functional workstreams to completion.

• Excellent written and verbal communication, including concise, tailored candidate outreach and clearly organized information.

• Strong attention to detail and data discipline, with discretion around sensitive candidate and business information.

• Ability to manage multiple searches, shifting priorities, and deadlines with follow-through and candidate care. Collaborative, proactive, curious, adaptable, and solutions-oriented.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office or comparable tools, and ability to learn applicant tracking, candidate relationship management, and research systems.

LLR Partners is a lower middle market private equity firm focused on investing in software and tech-enabled companies within the knowledge economy. Founded in 1999 and headquartered in Philadelphia, LLR has raised over $7.5 billion across seven funds and has partnered with over 130 companies. CDH 4C Medical Intermediate Unit

• 26 bed fast paced, mixed acuity Intermediate Medical Surgical UnitInpatient unit that provides care for patients with complex medical conditions, post‑operative needs, or clinical instability requiring continuous cardiac monitoring, frequent assessments, and timely interventions.

The Staff Nurse Inpatient  reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

A clinically competent, registered, professional nurse who prescribes, delegates and coordinates nursing care to the acutely ill patient through the nursing process of assessment, planning, intervention, implementation and evaluation.  Effectively interacts with patient, significant others, and other health team members, while maintaining ANA standards of professional nursing practice.

jobs.title: H&M Department Supervisor - Plaza Del Sol
jobs.description:
About the Role

As a Department Supervisor, you will be responsible for for supporting the Sales and Profit goals in the store by executing a plan to deliver the Best Customer Experience in the department and overall store. The Department Supervisor will work in accordance with legal requirements and H&M standards, policies, and procedures to meet the expectations of customers and colleagues.

A Day in the Life

Working at H&M means no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will include the following responsibilities*

Customer Sales & Profit

• You are responsible for supporting the total OMNI customer experience in your store, ensuring visual and commercial curation according to global guidelines.
• Representing yourself and the H&M brand positively during customer interactions
• Be aware of and take responsibility of your department's strengths and identifying commercial opportunities and working with your Department Manager to act on them
• Ensure customer service is provided in all areas of the store and that your team has the ability to work towards actively promoting and selling products to customers
• Following up that your team is actively promoting our Customer Loyalty App (Hello Member) & in-store sustainability initiatives
• Ensure correct routines in fitting room and checkout, including transaction, returns and exchanges
• Ensure all admin routines for both people and operations are handled in a correct way

Fashion & Trend Awareness

• Keep up-to-date with fashion scene, trends, tendencies, styles, brands, products, competitors and relevant influencers, etc
• Ensure your team provides product and fashion knowledge as well as other relevant information during customer interactions

Team & Development

• Retain and share your knowledge and skills with the Store team
• Collaboration, planning & teamwork with in-store Visual Merchandiser team
• Give & receive feedback with your colleagues to learn, develop & support each other
• Regular communication to store colleagues to inform, motivate and inspire – daily, weekly meetings, etc
• Ensure all procedures, routines, and legal requirements in all areas of the store are followed

Retail Operations/ Visual & Commercial Execution

• Secure a clean and tidy sales floor and back of house including stockroom areas
• Ensure high fashion quality, visual and commercial product presentation, with good garment care
• Secure good stock levels and provide input on allocation to Area team
• Ensure the full garment cycle – from delivery to garment presentation – and fitting room routines are according to our standards and routines set internally, utilizing all tools and technology provided
• Upkeep & follow best practice for any in-store OMNI Services & in-store tech services/tools, etc (Instore Care App, Click & Collect, Smart Store etc)
• Secure a strong balance and the maintenance of price signs in-store and throughout the sales floor/store following guidelines according to global and local strategies & sales market/regional requirements to ensure a strong and consistent price perception throughout store
• Updating & upkeep of BOH Areas for all colleagues (key information, health & safety, tidiness etc)
• Responsible for opening & closing of store daily

Who You Are

• To be a successful and effective Department Supervisor, you’ll be an emerging leader who enjoys taking responsibility.
• You must be ambitious, an effective communicator, supportive, an analytical solution finder, capable of working with numbers and managing statistics.
• You are achievement-oriented, motivated by performance and competition to be truly customer centric.

Why You’ll Love Working at H&M

• We value diverse backgrounds, including but not limited to race, ethnicity, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, and disability
• We pride ourselves on being a values-driven organization, guided by our 7 unique values that have been part of our success story for over 75 years
• You’ll have access to our Colleague Resource Groups (CRGs) to find community and networking opportunities among colleagues
• We are an inclusive company where you’re encouraged to be yourself at work
• You will have access to a large global talent community, where career growth and aspirations have no limits
• We believe in supporting your overall wellbeing and offer comprehensive benefits inclusive of health insurance, wellness and family support programs, company match retirement plan, paid leave programs, and paid time off, including a community day to serve your local community
• You’ll be able to express your personal style with our employee discount at H&M, & Other Stories, and COS

Compensation: expected base salary range is $17.05- $19.86 hourly**

EEOC Code: SLS

Pay Status: Non-Exempt, Hourly

*This job posting highlights the most critical responsibilities and requirements of the job and is not all-inclusive. There may be additional duties, and responsibilities assigned for this job at the company’s discretion.

**H&M, in good faith, has assessed this posted range of compensation as the accurate range for this role and location at the time of this posting. H&M may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range depending on candidate qualifications. This range may be modified in the future.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. If you require assistance or accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact us at https://hm.ethicspoint.com, and use Ask a Question.

Benefits:

We offer all our employees at H&M Group attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe. All our employees receive a staff discount card, usable on all our H&M Group brands in stores and online. Brands covered by the discount are H&M (Beauty and Move included), COS, Weekday, Monki, H&M HOME, & Other Stories, ARKET, Afound. In addition to our staff discount, all our employees are included in our H&M Incentive Program – HIP. You can read more about our H&M Incentive Program here.

In addition to our global benefits, all our local markets offer different competitive perks and benefits. Please note that they may differ between employment type and countries.

We offer: 25% Staff Discount - Medical, Pharmacy Vision and Dental Coverage – Employee Assistance Program - Vacation, Wellness, Holiday and Parental Pay – 401K – Commuter Benefits, Health and Dependent Care FSA. Plus, additional Voluntary Benefits.

Inclusion & Diversity:

H&M is a part of H&M Group. At H&M Group, we’re determined to create and maintain inclusive, diverse and equitable workplaces throughout our organisation. Our teams should consist of a variety of people that share and combine their knowledge, experience and ideas. Having a diverse workforce leads to a positive impact on how we address challenges, on what we perceive possible and on how we choose to relate to our colleagues and customers all over the world. Hence all diversity dimensions are taken into consideration in our recruitment process.

We strive to have a fair and equal process and therefore kindly ask you not to attach a cover letter in your application as they often contain information that easily can trigger unintentional biases.

Company Description:

At H&M, our purpose is to liberate fashion for the many. We want to shape a new world in Fashion. A world with one ultimate goal: to unleash your self-expression. As an H&M colleague, you’re encouraged to be yourself & more. You’ll take on new responsibilities from day one, learn skills for life, and find new ways to make your big dreams come true.

Our company is committed to fostering a culture of inclusion and belonging, and we actively seek colleagues who share our commitment.

jobs.title: Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner West Region Registry
jobs.description:
Northwestern Medicine is seeking on-call Sexual Assault Nurse Examiners (SANEs) for our West Region, supporting: Must meet on-call hours to be with-in 60 minutes of the following hospital.

📍 Central DuPage Hospital

📍 Delnor Hospital

📍 Kishwaukee Hospital

📍 Valley West Hospital

This specialized nursing role provides compassionate, trauma-informed medical forensic care to patients following sexual assault.

The Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner (SANE) reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

• The SANE (Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner) is a registered professional nurse who provides exemplary specialized, trauma-informed medical forensic services to all individuals who presents with a complaint or concern of sexual assault. These services will be prompt, non-judgmental and compassionate while encouraging autonomy and reducing psychological trauma. The medical forensic services may include a medical forensic exam and evidence collection, counseling for emergency contraception, prophylactic treatment for sexually transmitted infections, photo documentation, and referrals for appropriate medical and psychological follow-up, support and participation in legal proceedings.

Responsibilities:

• Acts autonomously following the professional standards as outlined by the Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act (SASETA), the Illinois Nurse Practice Act, the International Association of Forensic Nurses Scope and Standards of Practice, and unit specific protocols appropriate to the patient population served.
• Works collaboratively with the interdisciplinary team, including SANE coordinator, providers, imaging and therapeutic services to facilitate care of sexual assault survivor.
• Maintains documentation standards with accurate, timely and complete recording and reporting to ensure compliance with SASETA.
• Maintains appropriate survivor privacy and chain of custody for all evidence collected, including Illinois State Police Evidence Collection Kit (ISPECK).
• Remains up to date on current regulatory and legislative guidelines related to treatment and documentation standards for sexual assault survivors.

jobs.description:
Job Purpose

The Safety Coordinator is responsible for supporting the implementation and monitoring of health, safety, and environmental procedures within the Engineering Department, ensuring compliance with Accor standards, local regulations, and hotel safety policies. The position focuses on maintaining a safe working environment for all Heartists, guests, and contractors.

Key Responsibilities

• Monitor compliance with hotel safety procedures, engineering standards, and applicable local regulations.
• Conduct regular safety inspections of engineering workshops, plant rooms, equipment, and technical areas.
• Identify potential hazards and unsafe practices and recommend corrective actions.
• Ensure that preventive maintenance activities are carried out safely and in accordance with established procedures.
• Monitor compliance with permit-to-work procedures, including hot work, confined space entry, and work at height, where applicable.
• Ensure the proper use, storage, and maintenance of personal protective equipment (PPE).

• Maintain safety inspection records, incident reports, risk assessments, and related documentation.
• Report accidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions to the Chief Engineer and the relevant departments.

• Monitor the safe handling and storage of chemicals, tools, and engineering materials.
• Coordinate with the Security, Housekeeping, and Health & Safety teams on safety-related matters.
• Support internal and external safety audits and follow up on corrective actions.
• Promote environmental awareness, energy efficiency, and sustainable engineering practices in line with Accor standards.
• Perform any other duties assigned by the Chief Engineer or Director of Engineering.

Qualifications

• Diploma or degree in Engineering, Occupational Health and Safety, or a related field is an advantage.
• Previous experience in engineering operations, safety coordination, or a similar role is preferred.
• Knowledge of workplace safety procedures, risk assessments, and preventive maintenance practices.
• Familiarity with fire safety, emergency procedures, and the proper use of PPE.
• Good communication, organizational, and reporting skills.
• Basic computer skills and the ability to maintain accurate records.

Competencies

• Safety awareness and risk management.
• Attention to detail.
• Teamwork and collaboration.
• Planning and organization.
• Problem-solving.

• Commitment to Accor's health, safety, and environmental standards.

jobs.title: Logistics & Asset Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




THE DATA CENTER OPERATIONS TEAM

Examples of key problems the team is working on

 - Operate at the scale of a nation, not a building. Accelerating toward 10s to 100s of GWs by the end of the decade, more than the entire electricity consumption of many countries. You won't just run a data center; you'll run infrastructure the size of a G7.

 - Fly the plane while it's being built. Running flawless operations inside a live construction zone, adapting in real time and turning the pace of build-out into our advantage. You will redefine operational excellence.

 - Write the playbook, don't inherit it. Most operators step into someone else's system. Here you build one, leaving your fingerprints on how the whole company runs. As we scale 100x, you'll set the standards, shape the operating model, and grow the team by the thousands.


ROLE SCOPE

 - Own end-to-end logistics and asset lifecycle for a hyperscale data center site: receiving, shipping, asset tracking, and vendor coordination.

 - Maintain asset tracking from receipt through decommissioning, including tagging, labeling, and data entry in asset management systems.

 - Manage receiving and shipping: verify quantities, inspect for damage, and update tracking systems in real time.

 - Run cycle audits and physical inventory counts to hold 99%+ accuracy, and resolve shortages before they block build, repair, or deployment.

 - Fulfill parts requests from technicians and engineers fast, and keep staging areas organized for deployment, break-fix, and project material.

 - Process RMAs, warranty claims, and replacements with vendors, coordinate security escorts, and report on inventory performance, turns, and obsolescence.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would. https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c

 - You've owned logistics and asset management on-site in a data center, warehouse, or high-volume hardware environment.

 - You keep inventory accurate to a high bar (99%+) through disciplined cycle counts and real-time tracking.

 - You move material fast under operational pressure, so techs and engineers are never waiting on parts.

 - You manage vendors, RMAs, and inbound and outbound logistics end to end.

 - You build and report metrics (turns, obsolescence, accuracy) and improve the process from them.

 - Bonus: Asset management systems and barcode/RFID tracking. Data center hardware (servers, networking, GPUs). High-growth or hyperscale site operations.


SALARY & BENEFITS

 - Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

 - Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

 - Health, dental, and vision insurance.
   
   - Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.
     
     
     Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.

Physical Requirements

 - Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

 - Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

 - Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

 - Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

 - Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.



We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

jobs.title: Principal Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT BRANDLIGHT

Brandlight is the leading enterprise AI visibility platform, built to help the world’s leading brands understand, manage, and optimize how they appear across AI-driven search, commerce, and advertising.

As AI rapidly becomes a trillion-dollar marketing and distribution channel, Brandlight is defining the systems that decide how brands are surfaced, trusted, and chosen.

Join our team and help build the next generation of tools shaping the future of brand management in an AI-first world.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Principal Engineer who combines strong product instincts, deep engineering skills, and the ability to move fast without compromising on execution quality.

You’ll be a primary technical driver, taking significant product modules from concept through design, architecture, implementation, and production. You won’t just implement finished specifications, you’ll partner with product and design to shape the solution, make technical decisions, and own delivery end to end.

Your work will turn complex, large-scale data into fast, intuitive products for Fortune 500 marketing teams. You’ll build across the data and application stack - from data ingestion and ETL pipelines to scalable backend services and the APIs that power our product experience. This role combines strong backend development with hands-on data engineering, owning how data is collected, transformed, stored, and served to make exploring datasets with billions of records feel effortless. Whether your strength is backend or full-stack, you’ll have room to contribute across the product.

This is a hands-on role for someone who has driven meaningful product development in a fast-growing startup and is comfortable taking ownership before every requirement has been defined.

Responsibilities

 - Own complete product modules from concept to production.

 - Build and own production data pipelines.

 - Design scalable data models and APIs.

 - Build fast, reliable services that power data-intensive product experiences.

 - Drive performance across the system, from data layer to user experience.

 - Ensure data quality and reliability.

 - Create reusable product foundations.

 - Own production reliability and safe delivery.

 - Lead through hands-on execution.

Requirements

 - 5+ years of experience as a backend or full-stack engineer, building and shipping data-intensive production web applications, with strong hands-on backend development skills.

 - A proven track record as a primary technical driver at a fast-growing startup.

 - Strong backend engineering skills, including API design, service architecture, caching, asynchronous processing, and integrating external systems.

 - Hands-on data engineering experience, including building, deploying, and maintaining production ETL/ELT pipelines.

 - Strong SQL and data modeling skills, with experience preparing and serving large datasets for analytical workloads.

 - Demonstrated ability to diagnose and improve performance across the system.

 - Experience deploying and operating applications and data pipelines in a cloud environment, including CI/CD, automated testing, containerization, logging, monitoring, and production debugging.

 - Strong product judgment, clear communication, and proactive ownership.

Nice to Have

 - Frontend experience building polished, data-intensive interfaces and visualizations.


WHY JOIN US

At Brandlight, you’ll build and shape a new category at the intersection of AI, marketing, and commerce.

We’re a fast-growing startup led by repeat entrepreneurs, world-class engineers, and marketing leaders, all driven to reinvent how brands are built, discovered, and chosen in the age of AI.

Please only apply if you have unrestricted right to work in the United Kingdom. We do not have any opportunities for sponsorship.

We are looking for a Food & Beverage Team Leader who is passionate about hospitality, people and creating exceptional guest experiences.

This is a hands-on leadership role where you will be responsible for setting the standard for our Food & Beverage operation and inspiring the team to consistently deliver it. From breakfast in the Orangery, and dinner service in Carter & Fitch Smokehouse & Pizzeria, to busy weddings, banquets and events, you will be at the heart of the guest experience and will lead from the front.

You will take real ownership of the team’s performance. A key part of the role will be constant coaching, training and development, ensuring every member of the team understands what great service looks like, has the knowledge and confidence to deliver it, and is held accountable when standards are not met.

You will also have a strong commercial focus. We want our supervisors to understand that great hospitality and revenue generation go hand in hand. You will actively encourage the team to maximise every opportunity to increase Food & Beverage revenue through upselling, recommendations, promotions and outstanding service that encourages guests to spend more and return again.

The role requires complete flexibility. As a Duty Manager, you will take responsibility for the entire hotel operation, including our Food & Beverage outlets, Montana Spa & Leisure Club and Golf Course. You will be the senior manager on duty, dealing confidently with guest requirements, operational challenges, emergencies and unexpected situations while ensuring the hotel continues to deliver an exceptional experience.

You will be expected to:

• Lead, motivate, coach and hold the Food & Beverage team accountable for their performance and standards.
• Take ownership of continuous team training, ensuring colleagues are confident, knowledgeable and capable of delivering exceptional service.
• Lead by example and be prepared to get stuck in wherever the operation needs you.
• Drive Food & Beverage revenue by ensuring the whole team actively identifies and maximises sales opportunities.
• Deliver exceptional customer service across restaurant, bar, breakfast, banqueting, conferences, weddings and events.
• Ensure all Food & Beverage areas consistently meet Mercure and hotel brand standards.
• Work closely with the Kitchen team to ensure food quality, presentation and service are consistently excellent.
• Communicate effectively with the wider hotel team to ensure a seamless guest journey.
• Deal confidently and professionally with guest feedback, requests and complaints, resolving issues wherever possible.
• Take responsibility for the hotel as Duty Manager, overseeing the wider operation including Reception, Housekeeping, Montana Spa & Leisure Club and Golf Course.
• Make confident operational decisions in the absence of the General Manager.
• Ensure compliance with all hotel security, fire, health & safety and licensing requirements.
• Monitor cleanliness, maintenance and presentation throughout the operation and ensure issues are acted upon promptly.
• Be completely flexible to the needs of the business, including evenings, weekends, weddings, functions and busy periods.

This is a role for someone who wants to make a genuine difference — to our guests, to our team and to the commercial performance of the hotel.

We are looking for someone who combines genuine hospitality with strong leadership and commercial awareness.

You will already have:

• Previous Food & Beverage experience as Head Server, Team Leader or equivalent level.
• A genuine passion for delivering exceptional customer service and creating memorable guest experiences.
• Experience of coaching, training and developing team members, with the confidence to address poor performance and hold people accountable.
• A strong understanding of Food & Beverage operations across restaurants, bars, banqueting, conferences, weddings and events.
• The confidence and commercial awareness to drive revenue through upselling and engaging with guests.
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build strong relationships with both guests and colleagues.
• The ability to remain calm, organised and decisive when dealing with pressure or unexpected situations.
• A positive, energetic and "can-do" attitude, with a willingness to lead from the front and get involved.
• The flexibility to work across different areas of the hotel and at different times according to business requirements.
• The confidence to take responsibility as Duty Manager for the wider hotel operation, including Food & Beverage, Montana Spa & Leisure Club and Golf Course.
• Strong attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining high standards.
• The ability to work independently while also being a strong team player.

Most importantly, you will be someone who cares about people, cares about standards and takes pride in getting things right.

At Mercure Newcastle, George Washington Hotel, Golf & Spa, no two days are the same. You could be leading a busy breakfast service one morning, coordinating a wedding or large event that evening, and taking responsibility for the entire hotel as Duty Manager the following day.

We are part of the Accor family, giving you access to a global network of hotels, learning opportunities and career development. Our Employee Benefit Card also gives you discounted rates across Accor worldwide, alongside a range of hotel-specific benefits.

We are committed to developing our people and giving talented individuals the opportunity to progress. Through our learning programmes, you will have access to opportunities to develop your skills and earn qualifications while you work.

We are an inclusive company and our ambition is to attract, recruit and promote diverse talent. We believe that great hospitality comes from great people, and we want everyone in our team to feel valued, supported and able to be themselves at work.

jobs.title: Manager Growth Performance and Marketing Analytics
jobs.description:
The Manager, Growth Performance & Marketing Analytics is responsible for leading day-to-day performance analysis across Marketing and translating data into clear business recommendations. This role connects marketing activity, customer behavior, digital performance, CRM engagement, media effectiveness, and business outcomes to help the organization understand what is happening, why it is happening, and what actions should be taken.

This role serves as the primary business translator within the Marketing Insights & Optimization team, partnering closely with Brand, Growth Marketing, Digital Experience, Finance, Business Intelligence, agencies, and external partners. The Manager is expected to frame the right business questions, prioritize analytical work, guide the Data Scientist and Analyst, and deliver executive-ready insights that improve marketing effectiveness, customer growth, and investment decisions.

•Lead weekly and monthly marketing performance analysis across demand, traffic, conversion, appointment booking, media, CRM, ecommerce, and customer behavior.

•Translate complex data and performance signals into clear executive narratives, root-cause insights, and recommended actions.

•Partner with Growth Marketing to evaluate media, CRM, campaign, audience, and channel performance and identify opportunities to improve acquisition, retention, and customer value.

•Partner with Digital Experience and Brand teams to connect digital behavior, customer journey insights, and performance trends to customer experience and brand priorities.

•Prioritize and manage analytical work across the Growth Performance & Marketing Analytics team, including work performed by the Data Scientist and Marketing Measurement Analyst.

•Support marketing planning and investment discussions by providing performance trends, opportunity sizing, scenario analysis, and optimization recommendations.

•Help define marketing KPIs, measurement frameworks, dashboards, and recurring performance reporting standards.

•Partner with Finance and Business Intelligence to leverage source-of-truth data while maintaining clear ownership of marketing-specific interpretation, diagnosis, and recommendations.

•Use and interpret data from key marketing and digital platforms, including GA4, Adobe Analytics, Adobe Experience Platform / CDP, Adobe Journey Optimizer, CRM platforms, media platforms, and business intelligence tools.

•Lead, coach, and develop analytical talent, building stronger business acumen, storytelling, and recommendation-development capability within the team.

Education

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Marketing, Analytics, Business, or related field. (Required)

Experience

• 7+ years of experience in marketing, growth, digital, ecommerce, CRM, media, or business performance analytics. (Required)
• Experience supporting consumer-facing businesses such as retail, ecommerce, healthcare, multi-location, or agency/consulting environments. (Preferred)

Skills

• Strong Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) experience, including applying MMM insights to marketing investment and optimization decisions. (Required)
• Strong Power BI experience, including building and interpreting dashboards and performance reporting. (Required)
• Experience with advanced marketing measurement, including incrementality, geo-testing, lift studies, holdouts, attribution, and customer journey analysis. (Required)
• Strong understanding of marketing KPIs, customer acquisition, conversion, retention, revenue, and marketing effectiveness. (Required)
• Ability to translate complex data into clear business insights, recommendations, and executive-ready narratives. (Required)
• Experience with web/digital analytics platforms such as Adobe Analytics/CJA or GA4 and working with CRM, media, and customer data. (Required)
• Experience with SQL, Adobe Experience Platform/CDP, paid media platforms, or marketing measurement tools. (Preferred)

Taking Care of our People!

We understand the importance of financial health and security, and because of that, we provide competitive compensation to all Associates. We also offer a comprehensive benefits package including health and dental insurance, 401k retirement savings with company match, flex spending account, paid personal time off, paid company holidays, parental leave, employee eyewear discount and much, much more. jobs.title: Engineering Operations Lead - Configuration Management & Tools
jobs.description:
At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.


ROLE OVERVIEW

Every part on a Seaglider has a story: who designed it, what revision was approved, what changed and why, and which one the shop floor built. As REGENT grows from prototype to certified production and moves our Viceroy program through certification, that story has to be true, complete, and available to everyone who needs it — engineers, manufacturing, and the regulators who will certify the vehicle. We're hiring an Engineering Operations Lead to build the configuration management discipline that scales with us, and to own the engineering toolchain that enforces it.

You'll define and run REGENT's configuration and change management process: baselines, release workflows, the change control board, and the record of what is released and why — built for a growing engineering organization and for the regulatory path ahead. You'll own the hardware engineering toolchain — Siemens Teamcenter (with NX and Capital), and our Jira/Confluence standards — administering it, setting the rules, and keeping it a system engineers trust rather than a hurdle they route around. And you'll define how released drawings and bills of materials flow from PLM into our manufacturing execution system, so Manufacturing builds to the right revision from a single source of truth.

Success looks like a Viceroy with a defensible design baseline, a change process that reaches effectivity decisions in days rather than weeks, a Teamcenter environment run as a service to the engineering team, and a shop floor that pulls from PLM. It looks like the Chief Engineer, Manufacturing, and Certification all agreeing on what "released" means — because you wrote it down and built the tools to enforce it.

This is a builder's role. You'll establish the CM function at REGENT with direct partnership from the VP of Programs, the Chief Engineer, and the CTO's engineering-lifecycle team, and shape it for the team we're becoming. If you have lived in the seam between engineering and manufacturing, if you can hold a release on procedure and then help the engineer get it through the same afternoon, and if you want to shape how a new class of vehicle gets designed, changed, and built — we want to hear from you.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own configuration management for REGENT's programs. Author and maintain the Configuration Management Plan, define HW/SW/System baselines, and act as Release Manager for the Viceroy program — the procedural authority on what is released, in-work, or obsolete.

 - Stand up and run the change process. Write the Engineering Change Process (ECR → impact assessment → CCB → ECO → ECN), charter and run the Change Control Board across Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Certification, and drive effectivity decisions.

 - Own the hardware engineering toolchain. Administer Siemens Teamcenter (Active Workspace, workflows, roles, attributes, release statuses) with NX and Capital integrations; own Jama’s connection to other tools; set Jira/Confluence configuration standards; manage the engineering vendor and integrator relationships.

 - Define the engineering-to-manufacturing data contract. Specify which released items, attributes, and BOM structures flow from Teamcenter into the manufacturing execution system, how engineering changes propagate, and how as-designed and as-built are reconciled — in partnership with the MES implementation lead.

 - Finish the standards Viceroy needs. Part numbering, attribute standards, CAD and data structure, role assignments, and drawing/BOM release workflows — agreed cross-functionally and configured in the tools before design work depends on them.

 - Manage engineering licenses and tool access. Inventory, allocation, renewals, and audit evidence for the engineering software estate.

 - Prepare for configuration audits. Build the status accounting and audit approach (FCA/PCA) that certification will require on the path from PDR to CDR and first article.



WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Configuration management depth on hardware development programs — identification, change control, status accounting, and audit, applied through formal design gates and into production.

 - Hands-on PLM administration, ideally Siemens Teamcenter: item and revision lifecycles, release workflows and signatories, BOM structures, effectivity and revision rules, role-based access, attribute and LOV configuration. Strong Windchill, 3DEXPERIENCE, or Aras experience is welcome if you've shown you can learn a second platform fast.

 - Experience connecting engineering data to manufacturing — drawing and BOM release into MES or ERP, and a clear-eyed view of what breaks when part numbering, revisions, or ECO effectivity are wrong.

 - Requirements and traceability tooling (Jama, DOORS, or similar) and how it ties to baselines and change.

 - A track record of writing process people actually follow — plans, state diagrams, checklists — and of running a change board with senior engineers and manufacturing leads in the room.

 - Credibility on both sides of the wall. You've been trusted by engineers and by manufacturing, and you know when to hold the line and when to help.

 - Comfort as the only CM person in the building, setting priorities from program milestones and building what's missing.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.

 - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds.

 - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat.

 - Innovative Mindset: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance.

 


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation including a robust equity incentive plan.

 - Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance - we cover 100% of your premiums.

 - 401(k) with company matching, so you can plan for the future.

 - Generous flexible time off, paid parental leave, and company-wide holiday breaks.

 - Relocation packages available for those moving to join our team.

 - Daily, free catered lunches

 - Learning & professional development opportunities

If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact.

jobs.title: Manager, Electrical Engineering
jobs.description:
At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.


ROLE OVERVIEW

Seagliders are all-electric flying vehicles that operate on the water, bringing together complex electrical systems that need to work seamlessly, reliably, and safely. From safety-critical controls and high-voltage power distribution to electric propulsion, energy storage, electromechanical actuation, and harnessing, our Electrical Engineering team is responsible for designing and integrating the systems that make our vehicles possible.

We're looking for a Manager, Electrical Engineering who brings both strong technical depth and a passion for building, coaching, and leading high-performing engineers. This is a role for someone who can guide complex technical decisions, challenge designs, mentor engineers, and bring structure and clarity to a fast-moving development environment. You'll lead and grow a team of engineers, with responsibility for electrical engineering across multiple vehicle programs as we move from development and testing toward certification and production.

You'll work closely with your team to establish technical direction, navigate design tradeoffs, and ensure our electrical systems meet the demanding requirements of safety-critical applications. Just as importantly, you'll invest in the people behind the engineering — coaching engineers through technical challenges, providing thoughtful feedback, helping them develop, and creating opportunities for them to grow into stronger technical contributors and leaders. You'll foster a team environment built on clear ownership, collaboration, accountability, and continuous learning.

Reporting to the Director of Hardware Engineering, you'll partner closely with mechanical, software, systems, certification, test, and manufacturing teams to solve challenges that extend well beyond any single subsystem. You'll also play a key role in guiding our vehicles through major development milestones, including critical design reviews and flight testing. Success in this role means delivering technically sound, well-integrated electrical systems while developing a team of engineers who are growing in their capabilities, taking on greater ownership, and ready to tackle increasingly complex challenges as REGENT grows.

If you’re energized by working at the intersection of cutting-edge innovation, real-world impact, and hands-on engineering, you’ll be in the right place - and we’d be thrilled to have you on the team!




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead and Build the Electrical Engineering Team: Set technical direction, establish priorities, and guide engineering execution across avionics, power distribution, electric propulsion and energy storage integration, actuation, harnessing, and board-level hardware. Own hiring, performance management, and team development, creating an environment where engineers have clear ownership, make sound technical decisions, collaborate effectively, and are empowered to do their best work.

 - Drive Engineering Execution Across Programs: Translate vehicle and program requirements into clear engineering priorities, deliverables, and milestones. Balance competing demands across multiple vehicle programs, remove roadblocks, and keep the team focused on delivering high-quality designs through integration, verification, and testing.

 - Provide Technical Leadership and Oversight: Guide engineering decisions, challenge assumptions, and help the team navigate complex design tradeoffs. Lead meaningful design reviews, safety assessments, and technical risk discussions that identify issues early, strengthen designs, and maintain momentum without introducing unnecessary process.

 - Build Scalable Engineering Practices: Establish and continuously improve electrical engineering standards, design documentation, review processes, and verification practices. Partner with the team to develop the technical rigor, consistency, and documentation needed to support certification, manufacturing, and production readiness.

 - Collaborate Across Engineering and Operations: Serve as a trusted technical and organizational partner to mechanical, embedded software, GNC, systems, certification, test, quality, and manufacturing teams, as well as key suppliers and contract manufacturers. Drive alignment across disciplines, resolve technical dependencies, and ensure electrical systems are designed and integrated as part of the broader vehicle.

 - Anticipate and Manage Risk: Proactively identify technical, schedule, resource, and supplier risks. Communicate tradeoffs and potential impacts clearly, bring forward recommendations, and work with program leadership and cross-functional partners to resolve challenges before they affect major milestones.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Engineering Leadership and People Development: You've demonstrated the ability to lead, mentor, and develop engineers, whether through formal people management or technical leadership roles. You're excited to take ownership of hiring, coaching, performance management, and team development, and know how to bring out the best in others, build on individual strengths, and create opportunities for engineers to grow and take on greater ownership.

 - Strong Technical Foundation Across Electrical Systems: You bring deep technical expertise in at least two areas of electrical engineering, including avionics and data networks, low- and high-voltage power distribution, electric propulsion and energy storage integration, electromechanical actuation, or board-level hardware design. You also have a working understanding of the other disciplines, with the systems-level perspective and technical judgment to guide design decisions, evaluate tradeoffs, and lead engineers across multiple electrical specialties.

 - Experience Developing Safety-Critical Hardware: You understand how system safety, design assurance, environmental qualification, and regulatory requirements influence electrical hardware development. You're familiar with standards and methodologies such as DO-160, ARP4754, FMEA, or equivalent approaches, and know how to apply them to make informed engineering decisions.

 - Proven Experience Delivering Hardware Through Production: You've led electrical hardware development from requirements and architecture through detailed design, integration, verification, environmental qualification, and production readiness. You understand what it takes to move complex electrical systems from design into working, qualified hardware, navigate technical challenges, and deliver against demanding program milestones in aerospace, maritime, automotive, or other safety-critical environments.

 - Strong Cross-Functional Collaboration: You're comfortable working across mechanical, software, systems, test, certification, and manufacturing teams to solve complex engineering challenges. You build credibility through technical judgment, clear communication, and a willingness to listen, challenge assumptions, and work toward the best solution for the overall vehicle.

 - Experience Working with Suppliers and Manufacturing Partners: You've partnered with suppliers and contract manufacturers to define technical requirements, evaluate designs, establish acceptance criteria, and resolve issues throughout development and production.

 - Comfortable Building in Ambiguity: You thrive in environments where the technology is evolving, processes are still being established, and there isn't always a clear playbook. You can make thoughtful decisions with incomplete information, adapt as new challenges emerge, and aren't afraid to get close to the hardware and work alongside your team during integration and testing.



BONUS EXPERIENCE

 - Experience with Emerging Vehicle Platforms: You've worked on eVTOL, UAV, electric marine vessels, or other novel vehicle technologies, particularly in environments developing new approaches to propulsion, controls, or vehicle integration.

 - Hands-On Electrical Design Experience: You've personally designed or developed electrical harnesses, PCBs, or custom electronic hardware and bring familiarity with PLM and requirements management tools.

 - Passion for Aviation or Maritime: You have a pilot's license, boating experience, or a personal interest in aviation, maritime technology, or electric transportation.




WHAT WE OFFER

jobs.description:
ABOUT THE JOB

Do you know why Domino's Pizza hires so many drivers? Well, aside from the fact that our delicious pizza is the perfect solution for dinner for families all across the nation - we do it because we can. What do we mean by that, you ask? We mean that we offer a great flexible schedule that offers the hours you're looking for. That means you're free when you need to be. You'll have plenty of time left over for school, to hang with your friends, or whatever. Even if you need a second job for some extra cash, Domino's Pizza is the perfect place for you.

Right now Domino's is looking for qualified drivers to staff stores in your area. We're growing so fast it's hard to keep up, and that means Domino's has lots of ways for you to grow (if that's what you want), perhaps to management, perhaps beyond. Whether it's your hobby, main-gig, or supplemental job, apply online. We're bound to have just the thing for you.

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You must be 18 years of age and have a valid driver's license with a safe driving record meeting company standards as well as access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery. You should possess navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area and must be able to navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From delivery driver to management, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Make pizzas when needed and/or asked. Faster the pizza gets to the oven the faster it can get out the door!

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

· Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

· Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

· Must be able to make correct monetary change.

· Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

· Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

· Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

· Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

· Far vision and night vision for driving.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgements and decisions.

Valid Driver License (2 Years)

Valid Proof of Proper Automotive Insurance

Valid Vehicle Registration

Valid Food Handler Permit

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table. Delivery Experts must be able to sit in their car.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made three times a week and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

Standing

Walking

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Walking

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Climbing

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure To

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

Far vision and night vision for driving.

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You are responsible for everything that happens during your shift. This includes all cost controls, inventory control, cash control and Customer relations. You must set the example. You must follow ALL policy and procedures 100% of the time and expect the same from your crew.

In addition: Staffing, Paperwork, Cost Controls, Cash control, Food management, Work to a Schedule, Perfect Image and adherence to standards, Great Customer Service, Attendance & punctuality, Transportation to/from work, Store cleanliness, Marketing, Profitability.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From assistant manager to general manager, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

· Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

· Must be able to make correct monetary change.

· Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

· Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

· Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

· Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

· Far vision and night vision for driving.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgements and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

Start Driving Your Career With Domino’s!

jobs.title: Yard Driver- CDL-A
jobs.description:
Reposition company commercial tractors and trailers on designated non-highway areas [the yard] to include backing trailers to dock doors. May be required to shuttle tractor/trailer to and from logistic/lease companies.

We are hiring two Yard Drivers for flexible, full‑time schedules.

Schedule:

• Work any 5 days between Sunday and Friday
• Shifts are work‑until‑finished (end times may vary)

Shift:

• 1st Shift: Start time 5:00 AM
• 2nd shift: Start time: 9am or 10am.

Pay:

• $26.00 per hour (Bi‑weekly pay)

RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES

Moving and Operation of Tractor/Trailer

• Walk the yard to identify and document [in the DVCR booklet] vehicle defects.
• Communicate maintenance needs to Transportation Manager [Daily]
• Obtain tractor/trailer list from Transportation, record odometer, hub readings, and engine hours from equipment, and send to lease company [Weekly]
• Ensure trailers loaded with refrigerated products, i.e., cheese, chicken, etc., are at an adequate temperature.
• Ensure Warehouse Team Members have trailers to unload and/or load
• Assist with the unloading of trailers when necessary
• Reposition tractor/trailers on the yard to and from docks
• Comply with Domino’s Chock, Safety Cone, and Dock Signal Light policy
• Shuttle tractor/trailers to and from the logistic supplier
• Take trailers to be washed and cleaned
• Assist with backhauls
• May be assigned to assist Drivers on a designated route(s) to unload products to Domino's stores.
• Listen to and timely assist management and Drivers
• Required to always wear and follow Domino’s uniform standards
• Attend scheduled safety, team meetings, and training sessions
• Follow all local, state, federal, and Domino's safety rules, policies, and procedures
• Attend classroom instruction facilitated by the Transportation Manager, which covers Domino’s Chock, Safety Cone and Dock Signal Light Policy, Accident Procedure Policy, and any other pertinent policy and/or instruction information.

Complete Necessary Paperwork

• Maintain DVIR booklets
• Comply with DOT log regulations
• Accountable for the vehicle and product
• Clock in and out in timekeeping and People Net system

• High School Diploma or GED
• Must be at least 21 years of age
• Six months of verifiable CMV driving experience, one year preferred
• Must have valid Class A Commercial Driver’s License [CDL] w Air Brakes
• Must maintain a DOT Med Cert
• Must always meet the defined MVR standards to remain qualified to drive company commercial motor vehicle
• Must successfully pass a background check every third year on your anniversary date
• Must be available to work a flexible schedule, including but not limited to nights, weekends, and holidays, as well as a short notice on occasion

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

• Ability to stand and/or walk for long periods of time, climb stairs, and lift to 50 lbs. frequently and 100 lbs. on occasion, perform heavy pushing/pulling of product, work in refrigerated conditions [33-38 degrees], outdoor weather [rain, sleet, heat, snow, etc.], and work in an environment with exposure to loud machinery, when necessary.

Domino's offers:

• Competitive wages
• Paid Holidays and Vacation
• Positive work environment
• Comprehensive benefits available, effective first date of employment, including: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K with employer match contribution up to 5%, Paid Time Off (PTO), Paid Sick Time (PST), Short Term Disability, Employee Stock Payroll Deduction Plan, and Parental Leave.
• 401k matching contributions
• 15% off the purchase price of stock
• Company bonus
• Referral bonuses
• Career growth!
