jobs.title: Energetics Tool Engineer (Level V)
jobs.description:
Voyager is an innovative defense, national security and space technology company committed to advancing and delivering transformative, mission-critical solutions. We tackle the most complex challenges to unlock new frontiers for human progress, fortify national security, and protect critical assets to lead in the race for technological and operational superiority from ground to space.

Forge the Future: Join Voyager Technologies

The future belongs to those who build it. At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart.

You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Join a culture where innovation thrives, curiosity is rewarded, and impact is real. We’re a company of doers, thinkers and builders, united by purpose and grounded in reality.

If you want to put your skills to work where the stakes are real and the mission is bigger than any one person, forge the future with Voyager.

The Energetics Tool Engineer (Level V) for solid rocket motor (SRM) and aerospace propulsion programs is responsible for the concept, design, engineering, fabrication drawings, inspection requirements, procurement requirements, verification requirements, and fabrication support for tooling and equipment used in the manufacturing of solid rocket motors specifically energetic operations.

The position reports to the Special Tooling Group Manager and is part of Strategic Systems Operations based in Folsom, CA. This role is onsite or hybrid based in Folsom, CA; Reno, NV

In this role, the essential functions are:

• Manage assigned tooling projects by coordinating all design and fabrication activities to meet the program cost and schedule requirements. Travel to suppliers to support them as needed during fabrication and inspection.

• Work alongside the manufacturing team to ensure overall program quality, delivery, and cost objectives are achieved. Work with internal customers to define tooling and equipment needed for new and existing programs

• Develop tooling concepts, creating/reviewing and improving manufacturing processes to meet customer requirements while ensuring tool designs meet environmental, health and safety requirements. Apply DFM/DFA, GD&T, and Value Engineering principles to balance precision, ergonomics, manufacturability, durability, and cost in tooling design.

• Deliver and maintain detailed tooling design documentation, including CAD models, drawings, specifications, and work instructions to ensure consistent quality and repeatability in manufacturing processes. Inspect tool configuration for drawing compliance, including fit, form and function. Perform stress analysis to ensure that tools are mechanically sound and safe.

• Review engineering drawings and designs for manufacturability. Support operations and process engineering in the use of all tooling.

• Support continuous improvement activities.

• Assist in the selection and implementation of PDM/PLM systems to ensure manufacturing consistency.

• Assist in implementation of an MES (Manufacturing Execution System) and/or CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System) and/or EAM (Enterprise Asset Management).

• Assist in the development of standardized tooling documentation, specifications, and engineering best practices across the organization. Mentor junior designers and peers in their design efforts.

If your experience aligns with our basic qualifications and you are inspired by our mission, we’d like to connect. If you don’t see the right role right now, Join Our Talent Community and stay connected as we continue to build what’s next.

• Bachelor of Science required in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or other relevant engineering disciplines from an accredited university. May consider equivalent experience in lieu of degree.

• Ten (10) to fifteen (15) years of tool design/engineering experience with emphasis in solid rocket live operations.

• Must have working knowledge of casting, curing, and cutting operations in processing solid propellant both tooling and equipment.

• Must have experience in the tool design of cast cores; cast distribution; stripping of cast cores; cutting/trimming of propellant both attended and remote; fixtures/stands used in propellant environments; lifting, handling and transport of loaded motors.

• Proficiency with CAD software for mechanical design (SolidWorks, NX, or similar)

• Strong working knowledge of GD&T (ASME Y14.5) and metrology principles

• Experience with Finite Element analysis practices

• Demonstrated ability to design and validate fixtures, jigs, and gauges for precision assembly and inspection.

• Experience with tooling materials selection, machining processes, and tolerance analysis.

• Experience in tooling configuration management and change-control processes.

• Previous use of a MES or EAM/CMMS system to manage tool fabrication and maintenance.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience supporting Missile Defense Agency (MDA) programs.

• Experience with SRM motor case, nozzle, or divert/attitude control systems tool design is desirable.

• Previous experience in designing tools for automation.

Travel, Physical and/or Government Mandated Requirements:

• Travel up to 15%, including the possibility of overnights within (the US) to support program needs and supplier visits.

• Ability to lift, move or carry items or equipment up to 50 pounds.

• Must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. DoD security clearance (U.S. citizenship required); active Secret clearance preferred.

• Ensure your recruiter knows the clearance needed and TA will add the required verbiage such as ITAR

The good faith base salary range for this role is $157,000 to $218,300 at the time of this posting. Where you fall within the range depends on your experience, skills, and location. This range reflects base salary only and does not include benefits or bonus/incentive. This range may be adjusted in the future.

Voyager offers a highly competitive total compensation package designed to support the well-being, growth, and success of our employees. Employees benefit from a flexible and comprehensive rewards program that supports both professional and personal well-being.

• Flexible Time Off (FTO), empowering employees to take the time they need to recharge and maintain a healthy work-life balance

• 401(k) retirement plan with a company match of up to 4% to help you build long-term financial security

• The opportunity to work alongside a highly talented team in an innovative, mission driven environment

jobs.description:
Job Title: Business Development Manager (Federal)

Company: Loenbro, LLC
Business Unit/Department: Sales/BD
Location: Region: West
Reports to: Director of Business Development
Employment Type: Full-Time
FLSA Classification: Exempt

About Loenbro

Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries, and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.

At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.

Job Summary

As a Business Development Manager at Loenbro supporting our federal division, you’re responsible for collaborating and working efficiently within the Sales and Preconstruction department to ensure federal project opportunities and agency client relationships are identified, shaped, and cultivated. You’ll initiate and cultivate correspondence with federal end users, contracting officers, prime contractors, small business teaming partners, design partners, and internal stakeholders to execute federal client strategy plans, capture plans, and internal preconstruction initiatives.

You're an individual contributor working in a team environment.

Role & Responsibilities

• Build new federal agency relationships and existing federal client expansion.

• Federal maintenance, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity/ Multiple Award Task Order Contract (IDIQ/MATOC) task order, and project lead generation.

• Execute business development strategy set for federal expansion.

• Support federal client and vertical industry strategy with key stakeholders such as Department of Energy (DOE), Department of Defense (DoD), U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC), General Services Administration (GSA), U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).

• Targeted industry events and conferences for company visibility.

• Support federal sales goals for revenue delivery and backlog growth.

• Make monthly client calls/visits to existing federal accounts, prime contractors, and new potential business (10+ per week).

• Manage lead generation and federal pursuit origination, from forecast to solicitation, in Salesforce.

• Develop & maintain relationships with agency program managers, contracting officers and specialists, small business (OSDBU) offices, prime contractors, architects, engineers, owner reps, etc. Incorporate these touch points into annual Account Plans in Salesforce.

• Facilitate business growth by working with business partners (suppliers, subcontractors, small business teaming partners, joint venture and mentor-protégé partners, technology providers, design-build partners, etc.).

• Manage federal client strategy and top target pursuits.

• Work with and support preconstruction on capture planning and project win strategy, including teaming, pricing approach, and discriminators.

• Monitor SAM.gov, agency forecasts, and market intelligence tools for sources sought, Request for Inquires (RFIs), and solicitations; funnel and filter opportunities to appropriate parties.

• Coordinate and plan details for client outings (event tickets, client fundraisers, etc.)

• Lead and facilitate targeted federal industry days, conferences, and trade shows (booth coverage and client meetings)

• Coordinate and plan details for targeted federal industry association events such as Society of American Military Engineers (SAME) and agency small business forums.

• Work with the Sales and Preconstruction team on federal prequals, capability statements, past performance write-ups, and Request for Proposal/Request for Quotation (RFP/RFQ) related deliverables as required, with attention to Federal Acquisition Regulation/Defense Federal Acquisition Supplement (FAR/DFARS) requirements.

• Develop federal capability briefings and direct maintenance work introduction packages for agencies and primes.

• Participate in community events connected to company philanthropy work.

Skills

• Deadline-oriented, self-motivated, and possessing the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously

• Strong writing capabilities, organizational skills, and follow-through.

• Working knowledge of federal procurement (FAR/DFARS, SAM.gov, set-asides, IDIQ/MATOC vehicles) or the aptitude to learn it quickly.

• Strong interpersonal skills needed to work in a diverse and fast-paced environment

• Knowledge of construction industry, federal procurement, and evolving trends.

• Exceptional customer service (internally and externally).

• Ability to be accountable and start and manage projects proactively without guidance.

• Industry knowledge in electrical, mechanical, soft craft, fabrication and/or underground maintenance within federal, DOE/DoD, or other government facilities.

• Experience with Davis-Bacon, Buy American, and federal safety, security and site access requirements, or with GovWin/SAM.gov market research tools

• Customer Relationship Management (CRM)/Salesforce system experience for tracking and organizing client and project opportunities.

Qualifications

Required:

• 2+ years of experience in business development, sales, capture or relevant role.

Preferred:

• Bachelor’s degree in business, construction, public administration, communications, or related field.

• Federal government contracting.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Work Environment:

• Indoor office setting with controlled temperature.

• Potential visits to outdoor industrial sites with exposure to weather extremes.

• Potential exposure to noise, dust, chemicals, or other environmental factors.

• Federal sites may require U.S. citizenship, background checks, badging, or security clearance eligibility.

• Travel requirements: up to 10% of time.

• Work schedule: 8AM – 5PM Monday – Friday or as needed for company, client or industry events.

• Demonstrate, advocate, and embrace company values, LEAD: Live with Integrity, Exceed Expectations, Act with Urgency, Deliver Excellence.

This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro's Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) policies.

Benefits

Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team:

• Medical, dental, and vision insurance

• 401(k) retirement plan with company match

• Paid time off (PTO)

• Life and disability insurance

• Professional development and training opportunities

• Employee assistance program (EAP)

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked.

Guided by Core Values (LEAD), grounded in grit and a commitment to excellence, Loenbro betters our families, customers, and local communities.  If you’re ready to be part of a company that LEADS by:

• Living with Integrity

• Exceeding Expectations

• Acting with Urgency

• Delivering Excellence

…we want to hear from you.

Loenbro is an Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.title: Senior Technical Project Manager (Product Development)
jobs.description:
Founded in 2020, unybrands is the next-generation brand accelerator platform built to acquire, integrate, and scale digital-first consumer brands. Headquartered in Miami, with offices in New York, London, Berlin, and Shenzhen, our 240+ team brings deep expertise across e-commerce, brand management, consumer retail, operational scaling, and M&A.

Since inception, we have acquired 30+ brands across Pet Care, Personal Care, Home Care, Supplements, Baby & Juvenile, Garden & Outdoor, Sports & Fitness, and Home & Lifestyle — completing 20+ acquisitions and delivering 16 consecutive quarters of like-for-like organic growth post-integration.

Our competitive advantage lies in a fully integrated operating system purpose-built to transform digital brands into omni-channel category leaders. Powered by a proprietary technology stack built on NetSuite ERP with 200+ data integrations, our platform enables brands to thrive across marketplaces, direct-to-consumer channels, and brick-and-mortar retail.

We focus on acquiring digital-first brands within carefully selected verticals, then applying tailored value creation playbooks that drive growth through innovation, expansion, and automation. We believe the next generation of consumer brands will be built differently — and we're building the AI-enabled retail tech platform to help them consolidate and win.

About the Role

We're looking for a highly innovative, technically accomplished Senior Technical Project Manager with a passion for creating exceptional consumer products.

This is an opportunity for an engineer who loves inventing, solving complex problems and creating beautifully engineered products that people genuinely love to use. You'll work across a diverse portfolio of consumer brands and product categories, turning unmet consumer needs into elegant, differentiated products from initial idea to mass production.

One day you might develop an entirely new mechanism. The next, reimagine the ergonomics of an everyday product or solve a challenging manufacturing problem. You'll collaborate with global manufacturing partners, explore new technologies and bring creative engineering solutions to life.

We're looking for an engineer who can invent, develop and deliver. Someone who combines the creativity of a product inventor, the technical expertise of a seasoned mechanical engineer and the execution discipline of an exceptional project manager.

Much of our development is supplier-led, with manufacturing partners responsible for concept development, CAD modeling, prototyping and testing. You'll guide and evaluate their engineering work, challenge technical decisions and ensure products fulfill their promise. This isn't a traditional project management role. You'll own the technical development process and be accountable for getting exceptional products into production on time.

What You’ll Do

Lead Innovation & Engineering
• Translate unmet consumer needs into innovative, intuitive and commercially compelling product solutions.
• Invent mechanisms, improve ergonomics and solve engineering challenges through creative, first-principles thinking.
• Guide differentiated products across categories, balancing design, functionality, user experience and commercial objectives.
• Apply expertise in mechanical engineering, materials and manufacturing to achieve elegant, reliable solutions.
• Identify patentable innovations, develop invention disclosures and contribute to patent applications and IP design-around strategies with counsel.

Drive Product Development & Delivery
• Own concurrent NPD projects from concept through production, with accountability for technical execution andon-time delivery.
• Lead structured stage-gate reviews, decisions, risk management, cross-functional alignment and gate readiness.
• Manage schedules, critical paths and supplier commitments; resolve obstacles before they affect launch dates.
• Direct supplier engineering teams responsible for concepts, CAD, 3D printing, prototyping, engineering development and testing.
• Evaluate supplier designs, prototypes, recommendations and tradeoffs, providing clear technical direction.
• Partner with Sourcing, Quality, Compliance, Operations and Commercial teams to ensure successful launches.

Own Technical Excellence
• Create and maintain Product Specifications, engineering requirements, controlled documentation and design revisions.
• Write test plans and measurable acceptance criteria for performance, durability, reliability, safety and product
claims.
• Direct supplier and third-party testing; critically review test reports and drive corrective actions and root cause
investigations.
• Apply DFM/DFA across diverse materials, manufacturing processes and tooling technologies.
• Review supplier drawings, tolerances, materials, tooling and methods to optimize performance, cost and quality.
• Guide validation, pilot builds and production readiness, ensuring technical requirements are met before launch.

What You’ll Bring
Required
• Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related field; 8+ years of relevant engineering and NPD experience.
• Proven record of bringing innovative, mass-produced consumer products from concept to commercialization.
• Deep mechanical design, materials, tooling, manufacturing-process and DFM/DFA expertise.
• Success leading complex projects, stage-gate deliverables and on-time launches.
• Experience directing external supplier engineering teams across design, prototyping, validation and manufacturing.
• Ability to write Product Specifications and test plans, maintain documentation and evaluate technical reports.
• Experience with invention disclosures, patent applications and IP design-around strategies.
• 3D CAD proficiency; strong technical judgment, creative problem solving, communication and project leadership.

Preferred
• Development across multiple categories and manufacturing technologies; named inventor on patents.
• Experience with Asia-based manufacturers; familiarity with DFMEA, DVP&R, design controls and production validation.
• Advanced engineering degree or project management certification.

You’ll Thrive Here If You…
• Think like an inventor. You challenge conventional solutions and love making products meaningfully better.
• Have exceptional product instincts. You care about the details that make products delightful to use.
• Know how to get things made. You turn ambitious ideas into scalable, cost-effective products.
• Lead with technical credibility. You guide supplier engineers, challenge assumptions and make strong decisions.
• Own the outcome. You move with urgency and take pride in delivering outstanding products on time.
• Thrive on variety. You enjoy new categories, unfamiliar technologies and continuous learning.
• Bring an entrepreneurial mindset. You are resourceful, adaptable and comfortable with ambiguity.
If you’ve ever looked at an everyday product and thought, “I could make that so much better,” this is the kind of role where you get to do exactly that.

jobs.title: RevOps Solutions Architect
jobs.location: Remote - California, Colorado, Georgia, Illinois, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Texas, Utah
jobs.description:
About the job

At Go Nimbly, we want to be a global thought leader in the RevOps space by developing a badass brand built through innovative work created by individuals with growth mindsets. As a member of the Delivery team, you will help our clients drive more revenue by creating a buying experience that’s both frictionless and human. You will move these high-growth companies towards a more operationally efficient organization.

As a RevOps Solutions Architect at Go Nimbly, you'll collaborate with a team of RevOps Consultants, Program Managers, Developers, and Analysts to build best-in-class solutions and impactful technology roadmaps. You will act as a subject matter expert on the process of scoping, discovery, diagnosis, design, and leading the team through solution and architecture decisions by considering scalability, trade-offs, best practice, and the latest technology trends, including where generative AI can accelerate or improve general operations and go-to-market motions.

*Remote: Location Requirements

We’re a fully remote company. At this time, we are only able to hire candidates who reside in the following locations due to payroll, tax, and compliance requirements:

U.S. states: California, Colorado, Georgia, Illinois, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Texas, Utah.

Countries: Argentina, Colombia, Uruguay, Mexico, Brazil

As a remote first team, we rely on video calls to stay connected, make decisions, and work directly with clients, so being comfortable on camera and engaged in that setting is part of how we operate day to day.

On a given day, a RevOps Solutions Architect will spend time:

 - Shaping the approach early by leading discovery and scoping, making sure the work is estimated accurately before it starts.

 - Building connections between GTM systems that drive real value and outcomes, whether that's through custom code, integrations, or an iPaaS/automation platform like Workato, Make, or n8n. The tool matters less than knowing which one fits the problem.

 - Finding where AI and agents can add value, then building workflows that turn GTM data into actionable insights and automate work. You identify and propose when AI should own the process versus when a human needs to stay involved, all while respecting data privacy, security, and compliance.

 - Diagnosing where GTM systems are broken or fragmented, duplicate sources of truth, manual handoffs, data that doesn't reconcile, and owning the fix from root cause through to a shipped solution, not just flagging the gap.

 - Designing solutions for complex workstreams, advising clients on when to buy an existing tool versus build a custom solution, and presenting these solutions to client teams in a way that builds trust and makes the case for scalability and best practice.

 - Defining architecture principles and standards, and owning how design decisions are communicated and justified, both internally and directly with the client, including executive stakeholders.

 - Coaching and mentoring the team on solution design and championing diligently.

 - Keeping a pulse on the latest tech and AI releases to help shape Go Nimbly’s point of view on what they mean for clients.

What’s in it for you?

 - Flexible working environment: our entire team works remotely, and we have no plans to change this!

 - Tiered incentive program (in addition to base salary) to reward high performers.

 - Gain exposure to several high-growth companies looking to scale and invest in their revenue operations function.

 - Colleagues who are top practitioners. Many Go Nimbly alumni now lead RevOps and GTM teams at high-growth companies!

 - Annual camp: a yearly offsite to celebrate the year and plan the next one.

 - Dedicated to employee development and career paths aimed at fostering your growth and your career.

 - 100% paid premiums for US employees’ insurance coverage.

About you

 - You have 8+ years of experience in at least one core discipline (Sales Ops, Marketing Ops, or Business Systems) and working fluency across the others, including systems architecture and administration (Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, or similar), data modeling and integration design across the tech stack.

 - A genuine point of view on AI and agents in RevOps: judgment on where AI should own delivery versus where a person needs to stay in the loop, and mindful of data governance, PII, and compliance boundaries.

 - You work with senior stakeholders to uncover business requirements, diagnose gaps and pains, and design scalable technical solutions to resolve them, including advising clients on when to buy versus build.

 - Expert knowledge of Salesforce platform capabilities and core features, with a perspective on when to use out of the box features, declarative automation, or code, and comfort building connections across custom code, integrations, or an iPaaS platform like Clay, Workato, Make, or n8n.

 - A track record of diagnosing fragmented or broken GTM systems, duplicate sources of truth, manual handoffs, data that doesn't reconcile, and owning the fix through to a shipped solution, not just flagging the problem.

 - You can lead internal and client teams, hold your own in front of executive stakeholders, and explain technical decisions to both technical and non-technical audiences, with experience in lean and agile delivery.

 - Bonus: if you have a Certified Salesforce Application Architect or Systems Architect certification, or are on the path to achieving one.

About Us

We are positive people who have a sense of urgency, creativity, and decisiveness coupled with the willingness to work hard and well under pressure

 - Be a Leader. Leadership at Go Nimbly isn't about title, it's showing up with a point of view, saying the hard thing clearly, and making sure what you started actually lands.

 - Show Your Work. We love a finished product, but how you got there matters too. Clear communication and proactive updates are part of the job.

 - Value Long-Term Over Short-Term. The fast answer and the right answer aren't always the same. We're committed to building things that scale, even when that means slowing down.

 - Take It to the Finish Line. We don't hand things off and hope for the best. When you own something here, you own it all the way through.

 - Customer-Obsessed. When our clients win, we win. We genuinely understand their business and show up as trusted advisors, as invested in their outcomes as they are.

 - Gotchu Energy. The best teammates make the people around them feel like they've got backup, leaning into hard moments instead of away from them.

What’s next?

Apply! A real person on our Talent team reads every application. If we'd like to talk, we'll reach out. If not, we'll let you know that too, with clear feedback. Nobody likes being ghosted.

On the first call, our Talent team will walk you through the interview process. It varies by role and usually includes three to four rounds. We want to use everyone's time well and figure out together whether this is a good fit.

The base salary range for this role is $140,000 to $160,000 USD. Additionally, this role is eligible for a tiered bonus structure of up to 22 percent of base salary.

Initial placement within the range depends on geographic location, experience, and skillset, with most hires landing at or near the midpoint, leaving room for growth and future impact. The top of the range is generally reserved for those who are performing at a high level and impact here at Go Nimbly. Final offer amounts will vary based on leveling, and will be adjusted based on geographical location and the candidate's applicable experience and skillset.

jobs.title: Manager, Mid-Market Solutions Consulting
jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE 

As the Manager, Mid-Market Solutions at Ramp, you will lead and develop a high-performing team of Solutions Consultants supporting Mid-Market prospects and customers. You will establish the operating rhythm for a high-volume, fast-moving pre-sales motion; coach the team on discovery, demos, solution fit, and value-based selling; and partner closely with Sales, Product, Customer Success, Account Management, and Technical Consulting to deliver a consistent customer experience.

This is a player-coach leadership role. You will stay close to important opportunities while building a scalable team model: clear engagement standards, repeatable demos and discovery practices, strong capacity planning, and effective handoffs. You will use customer feedback and performance data to improve how Mid-Market Solutions Consultants help Ramp win, activate, and grow customers.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead, coach, and develop a team of Mid-Market Solutions Consultants; set clear expectations, provide regular feedback, and support career growth.

 - Establish a high-quality operating cadence for pipeline reviews, staffing, deal strategy, call coaching, performance management, and cross-functional planning.

 - Partner with Mid-Market Sales leadership to improve qualification, deploy Solutions capacity effectively, and build repeatable account and deal strategies.

 - Coach the team to run high-quality discovery, deliver tailored and efficient demos, connect Ramp’s products to finance and accounting workflows, and navigate solution-fit conversations with confidence.

 - Personally support the highest-priority or most complex Mid-Market opportunities, escalations, and customer-facing moments when needed.

 - Build scalable playbooks, demo standards, discovery frameworks, enablement assets, and knowledge-sharing practices that raise the team’s quality and speed.

 - Partner with Product, Product Marketing, Customer Success, Account Management, and Technical Consulting to translate recurring customer needs into clear feedback, strong handoffs, and improved customer outcomes.

 - Define and inspect team health metrics such as coverage, conversion, cycle efficiency, demo quality, solution fit, customer outcomes, and talent development.

 - Foster an inclusive, high-accountability culture grounded in customer empathy, collaboration, urgency, and continuous improvement.

 - Identify practical ways for the team to use AI to improve preparation, documentation, deal research, demo readiness, and customer-facing work while maintaining good judgment.


WHAT YOU NEED

 - 6+ years of experience in Solutions Consulting, Sales Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Professional Services, or a related customer-facing technical role, including 2+ years of people management or demonstrated player-coach leadership.

 - Proven success leading or mentoring teams in a high-volume SaaS, fintech, or other customer-facing commercial environment.

 - Strong understanding of financial operations, accounting workflows, and the needs of finance and operations stakeholders.

 - Working knowledge of business systems and integrations, including ERP, HRIS, identity, or accounting platforms; APIs and file-based integrations are a plus.

 - Demonstrated ability to coach others on discovery, solution fit, demo execution, commercial judgment, technical communication, and consultative selling.

 - Strong operating judgment: able to prioritize team capacity, inspect pipeline health, use data to improve execution, and make clear trade-offs in a fast-paced environment.

 - Proven ability to partner effectively with Sales and post-sales leaders while protecting customer trust and delivery readiness.

 - Track record of building repeatable team processes, assets, and rituals that improve consistency beyond individual contributions.

 - Excellent communication, organizational, and change-management skills.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience in fintech, spend management, accounting automation, payments, or adjacent financial software.

 - Familiarity with Ramp-relevant systems such as ERP, HRIS, identity, or accounting platforms.

 - Experience using AI-assisted workflows to improve solutions, sales, or customer-facing team effectiveness.

Now, we’re looking for an in-person Executive Assistant  to help our C-suite and team run smoothly from our San Francisco office.




ABOUT THE ROLE

In the EA role at Exa, you’ll support both our C-suite and broader team with operations, coordination, and scheduling. This is a highly variable, high-trust role where new and unexpected tasks come up often — you’ll be the connective tissue between leadership, the team, and the physical office. 

This role offers a rare, 30,000-foot view into the inner workings of a hyper growth startup—working directly alongside the CEO and executive team as they scale. You’ll be responsible for maximizing the founders' leverage across the entire organization—owning calendars, clearing bottlenecks, and making sure nothing falls through the cracks.

This is an ideal role for someone who thrives in ambiguity, operates with high agency, and wants a front-row seat to building an iconic company.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own scheduling and calendar management for our founders — anticipate conflicts, protect focus time, and keep the day running smoothly

 - Triage and manage executive communications — know what's urgent, what can wait, and what you can handle directly

 - Coordinate meetings end to end — scheduling, agendas, follow-ups, and making sure the right people are in the right room at the right time

 - Support senior recruiting — coordinate interview scheduling and onsite logistics for leadership and executive-level candidates, ensuring a world-class candidate experience

 - Help plan team events, offsites, and culture moments — from weekly team traditions to company-wide gatherings, you'll help make Exa a place people love to work

 - Continuously improve systems and workflows — you're not just running processes, you're making them better. Bonus if you enjoy automating parts of your own role

 - Handle the unexpected — You're ready for anything and energized by variety and ad-hoc tasks.


WHO YOU ARE:

 - 2+ years of experience in operations or in a similar role

 - Excellent communication and organizational skills - you can engage comfortably with leadership, candidates, investors, and partners

 - Strong ownership and ability to operate with little direction

 - Enjoy juggling multiple workstreams and fast-changing priorities

 - Strong people instincts — you know when to step in, how to help, and when to stay out of the way

 - Comfortable in a fast-moving, high-growth startup environment

 - Based in or able to relocate/ commute to San Francisco
   
   

This is a full-time, in-person role in San Francisco. In addition to premium healthcare benefits (medical, dental, vision), we also offer fertility benefits and a monthly wellness stipend to all of our employees.



Exa is an equal opportunity employer. Your Role at Raising Cane’s:

The Restaurant Leader is responsible for strategic direction for their restaurant and must maintain operations standards and drive results through people development, sales and profit growth. This role is tasked with teaching, modeling and upholding Raising Cane’s culture standards for all crewmembers, customers and partners.

The physical work environment includes working in a fast-paced kitchen environment (which requires extended periods of physical exertion, such as walking, standing, lifting and bending) and interacting with customers. It also includes both inside and outside work in varied temperatures, working with and around food products, common allergens, industrial equipment, commercial cleaning products that require the use of personal protective equipment and physical activities necessary to complete the responsibilities of the job.

Your Impact and Responsibilities:

Purpose of the position:

• Ensures overall financial success of the restaurant and is responsible for forecasting and budgeting
• Ensures overall restaurant compliance to company standards, policies and laws
• Hires and terminates management-level crewmembers including status change and payroll process
• Creates crewmember work and training schedules
• Develops management-level crewmembers including performance management
• Acts as manager on duty, opens and closes the restaurant, manages cash handling
• Monitors profit and loss statements, develops and executes strategy in all areas of financial and operational performance

General to the role:

• Enforces Raising Cane’s policies and standards
• Uses required tools, forms and logs to support shift execution, document results and take corrective action when needed
• Deploys crewmembers during a shift and provides exemplary customer service
• Utilizes reward and recognition program for the crewmembers in the restaurant
• Authorizes employee functions requiring manager approval (e.g. discounts, timeclock overrides, etc.)
• Ensures cleanliness of the restaurant and ensures the facility is in good working order

• Able to recognize problems, set goals, create plans and convert plans into action to solve problems
• Able to measure performance, subjectively and objectively with a high level of emotional intelligence
• Proficient in a variety of technology systems including Microsoft Office (Excel, Word and Outlook) and ability to learn and adapt to new systems quickly
• Able to work a variety of shifts including days, evenings and weekends and travel as needed for work-related functions and training

jobs.title: IT Manager (EMEA Remote)
jobs.description:
Location: Fully remote, EMEA timezone
Start date: ASAP
Duration: 6 months with opportunity to extend
Languages: Fluent English required




ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

Pragmatike is hiring an IT Manager to support the company's day-to-day IT operations and ensure employees have the equipment, accounts, and technical resources they need to work efficiently.

This is a hands-on operational role focused on equipment preparation, device configuration, user account management, access permissions, and basic IT support.

You'll be responsible for managing practical IT needs across the organization, supporting employee onboarding and offboarding, and ensuring that internal systems and workplace tools are properly configured and accessible.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Prepare, configure, and deploy laptops and other IT equipment for new employees.

 - Manage employee accounts, user settings, and access permissions across company systems and platforms.

 - Handle IT onboarding and offboarding, including account creation, access updates, and equipment collection.

 - Install, configure, and maintain software, applications, and workplace tools.

 - Provide first-level technical support and troubleshoot basic hardware, software, and connectivity issues.

 - Manage and maintain an inventory of company IT equipment and assigned devices.

 - Ensure employees have the appropriate access to internal tools, systems, and resources.

 - Maintain basic IT documentation, equipment records, and operational procedures.

 - Monitor equipment needs and coordinate device replacements or upgrades when necessary.

 - Coordinate with external IT providers when more advanced technical assistance is required.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Previous experience in IT administration, IT support, IT operations, or a similar role.

 - Good understanding of computer hardware, operating systems, and device configuration.

 - Experience managing user accounts, access permissions, and IT administration across different platforms.

 - Familiarity with Windows and macOS environments.

 - Knowledge of common workplace tools, SaaS applications, and account management systems.

 - Basic troubleshooting skills across hardware, software, and network connectivity.

 - Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

 - Ability to manage multiple IT requests and prioritize tasks independently.

 - Proactive, service-oriented approach with strong problem-solving skills.

 - Comfortable working remotely and collaborating with teams across different EMEA time zones.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 administration.

 - Familiarity with device management solutions (MDM), such as Microsoft Intune or Jamf.

 - Experience with identity and access management (IAM) tools.

 - Familiarity with IT asset management and inventory systems.

 - Experience supporting a remote or internationally distributed workforce.

 - Basic knowledge of IT security, device compliance, and access control best practices.




WHY JOIN US

 - 100% remote with the flexibility to work from anywhere in the EMEA region.

 - Hands-on ownership of day-to-day IT operations and employee technical support.

 - International environment working with a distributed team across different locations.

 - Varied responsibilities across equipment management, IT administration, and user support.

 - Immediate impact by ensuring employees have the tools and access they need to work effectively.

 - Six-month contract with the opportunity to contribute to the company's operational setup.



Pragmatike is committed to a fair, transparent, and inclusive recruitment process. We do not discriminate based on age, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

In accordance with GDPR, your personal data will be processed lawfully, fairly, and securely, and used solely for recruitment purposes, including sharing it with our client(s) for employment consideration.

jobs.title: STAT Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) $40-$45/HR
jobs.description:
Private Duty LPN STAT Opportunities throughout Passaic, Hudson, & Bergen Counties

As a STAT LPN with BAYADA, you'll have the opportunity to become part of our highest skilled nursing team, helping clients as they transition home from the hospital and filling last-minute openings. You'll be the first friendly face that puts new admission clients at ease right from the start. With your meaningful experience caring for people of all ages and acuity levels, you're ideally suited to provide the initial 4-6 weeks of skilled nursing care. Working closely with your Clinical Managers, you'll ensure each client's needs are met according to their care plan, all while delivering personalized one-on-one nursing attention at home.

STAT LPN Hourly Rate Range - $40.00 - $45.00

• Training Rate - $30.00/hour

• On-Going Case - $40.00/hour

• New Admissions - $43.00/hour

• Peer Precepting - $42.00 - $45.00/hour

Qualifications for STAT LPNs :

• Active New Jersey LPN license in good standing

• CPR Certified

• Willingness to work across market service area (Hudson, Bergen, & Passaic County)

• One year of skilled nursing experience

• Hands-on infant, pediatric, and adult tracheostomy and ventilator experience

• Commitment to a minimum of two twelve-hour shifts per week

• Commitment to work one weekend per month

What to Expect As A STAT Nurse

STAT nurses get paired with a new admission client and stay with that client on a consistent schedule for about one to one-and-a-half months. After completing this initial care period, you'll be matched with your next client. We offer traditional 12-hour shift options, focusing on hands-on care with one client. Clients’ ages range from infants to the elderly, with acuity requirements varying from basic care to complex needs such as trach and vent care. You’ll travel to your client's home, stay there for the full shift, and follow up with, execute, and properly document doctors' orders. Your responsibilities include performing assessments, monitoring clients’ conditions, and documenting observations, interventions, and evaluations—all vital to providing top-quality care.

Supported by a team dedicated to your success, our STAT Nurses enjoy:

• Preventive care coverage for ALL employees (PRN included)

• Medical, dental, vision, prescription coverage*

• PTO (paid vacation or sick leave) *

• Paid holidays, vacation, and sick leave*

• 401(k) with company match*

• Employer-paid life insurance*

• Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

• Scholarship opportunities, free courses, and on-the-job training

*Benefits subject to employment type

Keeping people safe at home and out of the hospital is more important than ever. BAYADA Nurses are Heroes on the Home Front, delivering the highest-quality private duty nursing care to help people live their best lives where they most want to be—at home.

If the hero in you wants to make a difference, provide meaningful one-on-one care, and develop relationships with both clients and team members, BAYADA has many opportunities and schedules to find your perfect fit.

Make your career what you want it to be

At BAYADA, we care for people of all ages, diagnoses, and acuity levels, giving you the chance to explore your interests and put your skills to work. Many of our adult and pediatric clients—infants to the elderly—require advanced care, such as tracheostomy and ventilator management. So, if you have high-tech experience, we’d love to speak with you! If not, we offer paid self-directed and tailored training to advance your skills to the next level.

Interested in pediatrics but never cared for children before? We offer paid training in pediatrics to prepare you to meet the unique and rewarding challenges of caring for children at home.

When your work matters, it matters where you work

Mission-driven and nonprofit, BAYADA has been at the forefront of health care for more than 45 years. We follow the highest clinical and safety standards, so we’ll prepare and equip our registered nurses to meet the everyday challenges of home care, and especially in this time of crisis.

If you’re the type of nurse who rises to the occasion, join our trusted team of home health care professionals who find working at BAYADA much more than a career—it’s their calling. Apply today!

jobs.title: Sr. RAN Software Engineer (Starlink Mobile)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. RAN SOFTWARE ENGINEER (STARLINK MOBILE)

SpaceX is developing a satellite-to-mobile network to deliver ubiquitous cellular connectivity worldwide through the Starlink constellation. We are partnering with mobile network operators globally to provide direct-to-cell service, extending coverage to billions of existing cellular devices. Starlink Mobile was designed to connect the unconnected, and this new product will greatly expand that mission by extending coverage to billions of existing cellular devices. Applications include connecting hikers in national parks, emergency responders, rural communities, remote sensors, and people in emergency situations.

As a Sr. RAN Software Engineer on the Starlink Mobile program, you will lead the validation and optimization of the 4G/5G RAN software protocol stack. This role requires strong software engineering skills to build scalable test automation frameworks and work directly with other software developers to triage and resolve complex 4G/5G protocol stack software issues.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Lead the design, development, and maintenance of CI/CD test automation frameworks for eNB/gNB feature validation, including functional, performance, interoperability, and regression testing

• Analyze UE and eNB/gNB logs to debug and root-cause RAN issues, and collaborate with developers to resolves issues and drive feature improvements

• Build software tools and data pipelines to analyze RAN performance and optimize eNB/gNB parameters to improve network KPIs

• Manage and prioritize network issues while collaborating closely with development teams to drive resolution

• Troubleshoot and maintain RAN lab infrastructure in collaboration with partner teams

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline

• 5+ years of Python/C/C++ coding experience

• 5+ years of experience developing, executing, and managing automated LTE/5G-NR test cases (including test planning and results tracking)

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• In-depth knowledge of 3GPP specifications and R17+ RAN features

• Experience with user equipment (UE) log analysis and associated software tools (QXDM/XCAL)

• Experience developing test automation frameworks or CI/CD pipelines

• Strong understanding of LTE and 5G-NR protocols with hands-on experience resolving software issues at the PHY, MAC, and RRC layers

• Experience supporting products through the full release cycle including commercial deployment

• Strong skills in debugging and performance optimization; exceptional analytical skills and engineering fundamentals

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 3: $175,000.00 - $280,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to EEOCompliance@spacex.com.

jobs.title: Spring 2027 Engineering Internship/Co-op
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SPRING 2027 ENGINEERING INTERNSHIP/CO-OP

SpaceX seeks extraordinary students to join us for engineering roles in Spring 2027. As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees who will help you apply your knowledge and grow your skills on projects that have a significant impact. You’ll also get to have some fun and network with other interns and employees through optional social and professional events. If you’ve demonstrated a commitment to academic success and motivation to apply your knowledge outside of the classroom, you are a great candidate!

Internships are available with a variety of engineering teams across the company including design, manufacturing and operations at Bastrop, TX; Bloomfield, CT, Brownsville, TX; Cape Canaveral, FL; Hawthorne (Los Angeles), CA; Irvine, CA; Long Beach, CA, McGregor (Waco), TX; Palo Alto, CA; Redmond (Seattle), WA; Vandenberg, CA; and Woodinville, WA.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program in an engineering, physics or math discipline by the start of employment

• 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable)

• Applicant for this intern position must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident (e.g., green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• GPA of 3.5 or above

• 6+ months experience of application of technical skills outside of the classroom (examples: laboratory, research, extracurricular project teams, volunteering, personal projects or prior internship/work experience)

• Ability to work well in an integrated collaborative team environment, including frequent interactions with technicians, other engineers, and managers

• Ability to work effectively in a dynamic professional setting with changing needs and requirements

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Able to work full time, onsite for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning in January or March 2027

• Able to provide own transportation for positions at Brownsville, Cape Canaveral, McGregor and Vandenberg locations

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay range:

Engineering Intern/Freshman/Sophomore: $28.00/hour
Engineering Intern/Junior/Senior: $30.00/hour

Your salary will be determined by academic level. Pay is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs, as well as access to our comprehensive medical coverage and a 401(k) retirement plan. Students joining SpaceX through our internship program will receive the opportunity to attend presentations from company leaders, social and networking events, as well as professional and personal development trainings. Interns are also eligible for paid company holidays. SpaceX offers 10 or more paid holidays per year.

PROGRAM DESCRIPTIONS:

VEHICLE

• DRAGON: The Dragon spacecraft is capable of carrying up to 7 passengers to and from Earth orbit, and beyond. It is the only spacecraft currently flying that is capable of returning significant amounts of cargo to Earth and is the first private spacecraft to take humans to the space station.

• FALCON: The Falcon program tackles space exploration’s toughest problems through the ongoing development of our reusable launch vehicles, Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy. These vehicles are currently responsible for delivering commercial, national security, and NASA satellites into orbit, as well as supply critical science, supplies, and crew to the International Space Station.

• STARSHIP: The Starship spacecraft and Super Heavy rocket – collectively referred to as Starship – represent a fully reusable transportation system designed to carry both crew and cargo to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond. Starship is the world’s most powerful launch vehicle ever developed, designed to carry more than 100 metric tonnes to orbit in a fully reusable configuration and powered by our Raptor and Raptor Vacuum (RVac) engines, which are designed for use in the vacuum of space.

SATELLITE / SPACEXAI

• STARLINK: Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, including thousands of satellites, consumer receivers, and the software that brings it all together. Our Starlink teams are also undertaking SpaceX's next-generation mobile network, Starlink Mobile, connecting human beings all around the globe anywhere they can see the sky.

• STARSHIELD - Starshield leverages SpaceX’s Starlink technology and launch capability to support national security efforts. While Starlink is designed for consumer and commercial use, Starshield is designed for government use, with an initial focus on earth observation, communications, and hosted payloads.

• SPACEXAI - SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. This includes Grok, the frontier AI model for everything you need, trained on the world's largest supercluster, and developing Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth.

jobs.title: Electrical Safety Engineer
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

ELECTRICAL SAFETY ENGINEER

The Environmental Health and Safety Business Operations team is seeking a highly driven electrical safety engineer to support how EHS runs electrical safety across SpaceX production, test, and launch infrastructure. This role builds and maintains the programs, procedures, training, metrics, and compliance processes the team uses to keep medium- and low-voltage power systems, manufacturing equipment, ground support systems, and construction power aligned with personnel-protection and control-reliability requirements as operations scale. The ideal candidate will have a comprehensive understanding of industrial electrical system architecture, NFPA 70E electrical safety work practices, and the hazards associated with switchgear, motor control centers, transformers, generators, temporary power, and equipment in hazardous locations.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Support the EHS Business Operations team in administering the electrical safety program in accordance with NFPA 70E, including shock protection, arc-flash protection, energized electrical work permits, approach boundaries, and electrically safe work conditions

• Develop, maintain, and control lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures, switching-order templates, and live-dead-live verification practices for switchgear, motor control centers, transformers, automatic transfer switches (ATS), generators, distribution equipment, and production and ground-support loads

• Coordinate arc-flash hazard analysis and incident energy studies (IEEE 1584), maintain equipment-labeling standards, and define PPE categories, working distances, and restricted/limited approach boundaries for AC and DC systems, including outdoor installations

• Support qualification, training, and audit of electrical workers as NFPA 70E Qualified Persons; develop electrical safety training content and tracking for operators, technicians, contractors, and construction partners

• Maintain the review and approval process for energized work, electrical switching, and commissioning procedures; define the criteria EHS uses to stop work when conditions do not meet electrically safe work practice requirements

• Maintain standards for grounding, bonding, equipotential bonding, lightning protection, and power quality monitoring so equipment damage and personnel injury are prevented

• Document and maintain generator, ATS, and backup-power transfer expectations for personnel safety during planned and unplanned transfers, including black-start, paralleling, and restoration during utility outages, storms, and site operations

• Partner with design, construction, and commissioning teams on behalf of EHS Business Operations to integrate electrical safety into new builds and expansions: one-line diagrams, protective device coordination, short-circuit studies, temporary power, and construction LOTO across production, test, and launch areas

• Run structured risk assessments of electrical systems, including Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and electrical hazard assessments for medium- and low-voltage distribution, classified hazardous locations, and high-energy equipment, and feed results into EHS risk and action tracking

• Support investigation of electrical incidents, near misses, shock events, and arc-flash events; track root-cause analysis and corrective actions to closure

• Track and report electrical hazards associated with hot work near energized equipment, cooling or ventilation failures, and environmental conditions that degrade insulation, PPE, enclosures, and equipment ratings

• Maintain safe operating limits and emergency response procedures for electrical events, including arc flash, shock, power loss, and fire involving electrical equipment, aligned with site emergency response and operational constraints

• Maintain compliance processes for applicable codes and standards, including NFPA 70 (NEC) as adopted by the applicable jurisdiction, NFPA 70E, NFPA 70B, OSHA 1910 Subpart S, IEEE, IEC, and hazardous-location requirements

• Coordinate with contractors, vendors, and utility providers so electrical safety requirements are enforced during installation, maintenance, interconnection, and repairs on power infrastructure

• Own electrical safety metrics, audit readiness, document control, and recurring business reviews so EHS leadership can see program health, gaps, and corrective-action status across supported operations

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, electrical and computer engineering, electrical engineering technology, or related engineering field

• 3+ years of professional experience in electrical power systems, electrical safety, or industrial electrical operations

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Direct ownership or administration of an NFPA 70E electrical safety program in an industrial, utility, manufacturing, or other high-hazard environment

• Hands-on experience in manufacturing plants, heavy industrial facilities, utilities, or large construction sites, including outdoor or harsh-environment installations

• Experience with arc-flash studies, short-circuit analysis, and protective device coordination using ETAP, SKM PowerTools, EasyPower, or equivalent

• Working knowledge of industrial electrical architecture, including utility feeds, substations, switchgear, transformers, motor control centers, generators, paralleling equipment, ATS, and temporary construction power

• Familiarity with delta/wye transformers, protective relaying, facility grounding, lightning protection, and power quality

• Experience with NEC hazardous (classified) locations and electrical work near flammable or energetic operations

• Experience creating and implementing electrical LOTO, switching procedures, and energized electrical work permit processes on active construction or operating sites

• Knowledge of OSHA 1910.147, OSHA 1910.269/1910.333, NFPA 70, NFPA 70B, IEEE 1584, and NESC as applicableNFPA 70E related certifications (e.g., CESCP, CESW, or equivalent electrical safety credentials)

• PE (Professional Engineer) license

• CSP (Certified Safety Professional) or equivalent EHS credential

• Proficiency in AutoCAD Electrical, Revit, or similar electrical design tools

• Proficiency with PFMEA, root cause analysis, statistical process control, and structured problem-solving methodologies

• Experience supporting an EHS or operations team with program governance, metrics, audits, training administration, or document control across more than one site

• Experience working with utility providers, electrical contractors, and commissioning agents on interconnection, cutovers, and live-facility work

• Ability to quickly assess an electrical issue and guide technicians through safe troubleshooting and repair

• Strong interpersonal and collaborative skills, enthusiasm for the mission of enabling multi-planetary life

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Relocation is required if not already local to a SpaceX site.

• This is not a remote or hybrid position

• Position requires the ability to travel and support critical infrastructure as needed

• Ability to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support construction, commissioning, test, and launch operations

• Must be able to work in industrial environments and comply with site access and safety requirements when on location

jobs.description:
ARS Pharmaceuticals is a fast-growing, innovative company dedicated to transforming the treatment of severe allergic reactions with neffy®, the first and only FDA-approved needle-free epinephrine product. If you’re motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and inclusive culture.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Manager / Sr. Manager, Technical Operations will play a key role in executing Technical Operations programs that support the continued development and commercial supply of neffy™. The successful candidate will combine strong technical judgment, project management, and external partner leadership in a highly collaborative environment.

Working closely with internal stakeholders and CMOs, this role provides technical and operational leadership across the ARS outsourced manufacturing network. Responsibilities include leading Technical Operations projects, supporting formulation and process development, technology transfer, GMP manufacturing activities, and resolution of technical and operational issues. The position ensures project scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, and budgets remain aligned while proactively identifying and escalating risks to support compliant, reliable, and on-time product supply.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Manage cross-functional Technical Operations projects and day-to-day technical and operational interactions with assigned external partners, including scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, budgets, risks, key milestones, project meetings, action tracking, scopes of work, proposals, change orders, and CMO/vendor performance metrics and KPIs (e.g., service, quality, delivery, capacity, and right-first-time).

• Serve as a Technical Operations point of contact for assigned external manufacturing partners and work closely with CMOs and internal stakeholders to ensure execution against agreed project plans and supply requirements.

• Provide technical oversight of formulation and process development, scale-up, technology transfer, process characterization, process validation/PPQ, and continued process verification activities, as applicable.

• Plan and support clinical and commercial manufacturing campaigns in coordination with CMOs, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and other internal functions; provide on-site/person-in-plant support for key manufacturing activities as needed.

• Review manufacturing and process documentation, including master and executed batch records, protocols, reports, process performance data, vendor change controls, investigations, and annual/product reviews, for technical accuracy and process performance.

• Lead or support technical assessment and resolution of manufacturing deviations, out-of-specification or atypical results, and other process issues; contribute to root-cause analysis and appropriate corrective and preventive actions in partnership with Quality Assurance.

• Assess proposed manufacturing and process changes for technical impact and support cross-functional evaluation of quality, supply, and regulatory implications.

• Monitor and trend manufacturing and process performance data to identify emerging risks, process drift, and opportunities for continuous improvement and operational excellence.

• Support vendor selection, onboarding, and qualification activities in collaboration with Quality Assurance, Supply Chain, Procurement, and other stakeholders.

• Communicate project status, technical risks, manufacturing issues, and recommend actions clearly to Technical Operations leadership and cross-functional stakeholders; escalate significant issues to appropriate decision-makers.

• Support preparation and review of CMC information for regulatory submissions and responses to health authority questions, as required.

• Support Technical Operations process improvement, business continuity, capacity planning, and other strategic operational initiatives as assigned.

• Support commercial supply operations managed within Technical Operations, including coordination with third-party logistics (3PL) providers, distribution partners, and external manufacturing/packaging partners to maintain reliable product supply.

• Support product serialization activities, including EPCIS data exchange and operational compliance with applicable Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) requirements, working with packaging, distribution, Quality Assurance, and other partners as appropriate.

• Support clinical supply activities, including coordination with Clinical Operations and external vendors for clinical packaging, labeling, distribution, inventory/expiry management, and Interactive Response Technology/Interactive Web Response System (IRT/IWRS) activities, as applicable.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

• Strong working knowledge of current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP), pharmaceutical manufacturing operations, and applicable quality systems and regulatory expectations.

• Demonstrated technical understanding of formulation, manufacturing processes, scale-up, technology transfer, process validation, and process performance sufficient to critically evaluate CMO data and recommendations, work effectively in cross-functional technical teams, and hold external partners accountable to commitments.

• Strong project and vendor management skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, timelines, deliverables, and external partners in a fast-paced environment.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate complex manufacturing or process issues, develop recommendations, and communicate the rationale for action.

• Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to communicate effectively across functions and organizational levels, including senior management and external partners.

• Well-organized, detail-oriented, and able to identify and escalate risks while maintaining focus on execution and business priorities.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project/reporting tools; experience with project management, continuous improvement, or operational excellence methodologies is a plus.

• Working knowledge of commercial and clinical supply operations relevant to Technical Operations, including 3PL interfaces, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA requirements, and clinical IRT/IWRS processes; direct experience in one or more of these areas is preferred.

• Must be able to travel domestically and internationally up to approximately 20% to support external manufacturing partners and key project activities.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

• Experience with drug-device combination products, nasal/inhalation products, sterile manufacturing, commercial product launch, or PPQ is preferred.
