jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
Program Manager

Miami (USA) preferred; open to other US locations

About Us

OpenFX is on a mission to move money as freely as data, unrestricted by time zones, banking hours, or legacy systems. We are building the infrastructure that will power the next generation of cross-border payment systems for institutions. The team's execution has been exceptional, and we're scaling at a remarkable pace. Our early team comes from companies like J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, FalconX, PayPal, Affirm, Polygon, Kraken, Nium and others. We're backed by Accel, Lightspeed, NFX and other top-tier investors.

Role Overview

Launching a new product or expanding into a new geography is one of the hardest things a cross-border payments company does. Each launch depends on licenses and regulatory approvals, banking and liquidity partners, compliance controls, settlement operations and go-to-market readiness. It needs coordinated work from nearly every function: Product, R&D, Legal, Licensing, Compliance, Trade Ops, Partnerships, Marketing, Sales and Finance.

We are hiring our first Program Manager to lead the cross-functional planning and execution of OpenFX's most strategic initiatives, turning company priorities into launches that meet their business goals. Working alongside Product, which owns the why and what, you will own the how and when: one plan across every function, the critical path through regulators and partners, and the trade-offs leadership needs to decide. You will be measured on outcomes: launches that go live on time, within scope, and hit their business KPIs.

This is a high-visibility role in Ops, working directly with the executive team. You will lead through influence rather than authority, and build OpenFX's program management function from the ground up as we scale into new markets.

Key Responsibilities

• Integrated planning Join initiatives at the idea stage, not at build, so cross-functional needs shape the plan instead of disrupting it. Build and own one integrated plan covering what, how, when and dependencies for every function involved. Map stakeholders and define team roles, and collect requirements from non-product functions early (compliance controls, licensing, reporting, operational processes) to prevent late scope drift. Plan in iterations, defining MVP, V1 and V2 so we deliver value to market fast, not waterfall.

• Operating rhythm Set up and run a lightweight "way we work" per initiative: kickoff, weekly cross-functional syncs, weekly status reports, monthly steering reviews and post-launch retrospectives. Keep the framework minimal: every forum and artifact must speed up execution, and you drop any that don't.

• Delivery tracking and risk management Track progress against plan, maintain the RAID log (risks, assumptions, issues, decisions) and remove blockers. Surface critical dependencies early: licenses, regulatory approvals, banking and liquidity partners, compliance requirements. Make scope, timeline and effort trade-offs visible early and bring options to the right owner for a decision.

• Launch readiness Own the readiness checklist and go/no-go process across all functions, from planning to launch. Run gate checkpoints with Product, so work moves forward only when every function has signed off on requirements, committed to the plan and confirmed readiness. Lead post-launch KPI reviews at 3 and 6 months.

• Transparency and stakeholder management Be the single source of truth for executives on status, risks and decisions needed. Partner closely with Product and function leads without standing between them; keep shared ownership of outcomes across the team.

• Building the function Design, roll out and refine OpenFX's program management framework with leadership and function leads. Measure the role on outcomes: on-time launch, scope delivered, effort vs. plan, fewer late surprises, readiness and business KPIs met.

What we are looking for

Must-haves:

• 7+ years of experience in program management, technical program management or similar cross-functional delivery roles, preferably in fintech.

• A track record of launching complex, cross-functional initiatives (new markets, products or regulated offerings) end to end.

• A goal-oriented mindset: you measure success by business outcomes and KPIs, not activity, and keep the team focused on what moves them.

• Strong analytical skills: you use data to set baselines, track progress, size trade-offs and back recommendations to leadership.

• Ability to lead through influence: aligning Product, Engineering, Legal, Compliance, Ops, Sales and Finance without direct authority.

• Strong planning skills: dependency mapping, risk management, readiness and go/no-go processes.

• A pragmatic, iterative approach; you know when process helps and when it slows a team down.

• Strong collaboration and communication skills: you build trust across teams and seniority levels, align people with different priorities, and communicate clearly in writing and verbally, from day-to-day updates to concise executive reporting.

• Comfort with ambiguity and a fast-paced startup environment.

What helps you stand out:

• Program management experience at a payments, FX, crypto or other fintech company.

• Experience with regulated launches: licensing, AML/KYC controls, banking or liquidity partner onboarding.

• Familiarity with FX markets, cross-border payments or stablecoin infrastructure.

• Experience building a program management function or framework from scratch.

• PMP, PgMP or similar certification (nice to have, not required).

What We Offer

• Competitive salary and benefits package.

• Equity in a rapidly growing company.

• The chance to build OpenFX's program management function from the ground up.

• Opportunity to make a significant impact on global financial infrastructure.

• Collaborative work culture with emphasis on personal and professional growth.

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

jobs.title: Enterprise+ Account Executive
jobs.description:
Gong harnesses the power of AI to transform how revenue teams win. The Gong Revenue AI Operating System unifies data, insights, and workflows into a single, trusted system that observes, guides, and acts alongside the world’s most successful revenue teams. Powered by the Gong Revenue Graph, AI-powered intelligence, specialized agents, and trusted applications, Gong helps more than 5,000 companies around the world deeply understand their teams and customers, automate critical sales workflows, and close more deals with less effort. For more information, visit www.gong.io.

At Gong, you will join a company built on innovative products, ambitious goals, and passionate people. We are shaping the future of revenue intelligence and we want people who are excited to build what comes next. You will work with a team that dreams big, moves fast, and cares deeply about the craft and about each other. Here, transparency and trust are core to how we operate, and every person has the opportunity to make a visible impact. If you want to grow, stretch, and do work that truly matters, Gong is the place to do the best work of your career.

We are looking for an enterprise seller who is ready to take their game to the next level. This is a hunt-to-own role: you win the logo, and you keep it. There is no handoff after the close. You own the relationship and grow the account over time. You have proven you can close enterprise deals and navigate complex buying processes. You build relationships at the executive level, create pipeline through your own initiative, and show up to every conversation with a clear point of view. You are competitive, curious, and disciplined, and you are looking for a platform where your best work will be recognized and rewarded.

Responsibilities

• Own a greenfield territory of enterprise accounts (4,000+ employees), driving net new logo acquisition from prospecting through close

• Build and manage a self-sourced pipeline — the majority of your opportunities will come from your own outbound activity, creativity, and relationships

• Navigate complex, multi-threaded sales cycles (9+ months) involving C-suite and VP-level stakeholders across Revenue, Operations, and Technology

• Develop tailored account plans that identify key buying stakeholders, decision processes, current investments, and expansion opportunities across the account

• Position Gong as a strategic platform — not just a product — by consulting on revenue strategy and helping customers understand the value of Revenue Intelligence at an organizational level

• Land new accounts and expand them, building a book of business that grows in value over time through a disciplined land and expand motion

• Partner with SDR, Sales Engineering, and Customer Success teams to build account-based strategies and deliver a seamless customer experience

jobs.title: Senior - Customer Solutions Specialist (Adelaide)
jobs.description:
About Netwealth

Netwealth isn't just a company.  We're shaping the future of wealth in Australia.  Our award-winning platform and NextGen technology empower advisers and investors to achieve more, and we're proud to be recognised as one of Australia's most innovative FinTech businesses.

Since 1999, we've grown rapidly by challenging the status quo. We move fast, think big, and stay agile.  Free from unnecessary bureaucracy so we can deliver smarter solutions for our clients and create real impact.

But what truly sets us apart?  Our people.  We're a team of curious, optimistic and courageous individuals who collaborate to make life better for more Australians.  We value authenticity, and agility, and we believe in creating an environment where you can do your best work, grow your career, and feel part of something meaningful.

If you're looking for  a place where your ideas matter, where innovation is celebrated, and where you can help shape a brighter financial future, join us at Netwealth.



The opportunity

We’re building a brand-new Customer Solutions pod in our Adelaide office, and we’re looking for an experienced Senior - Customer Solutions Specialist to be part of it from the beginning.



You’ll bring your experience in financial services, your confidence navigating complex customer conversations and your passion for finding the right solution. Along the way, you’ll have the opportunity to share your knowledge, support the people around you and help shape how our new Adelaide team works together.



If you know financial services, genuinely love helping customers and want your next move to feel like a step forward, this could be it.



What you’ll be doing

At Netwealth, Customer Operations plays an important role in delivering reliable, high-quality experiences for our advisers and clients across their journey on the Netwealth platform.



As a Senior - Customer Solutions Specialist, you’ll be one of the experienced members of our new Adelaide pod.

You’ll:

 - Support clients and advisers across phone, email and online chat

 - Manage a broad range of product, service and general enquiries

 - Take ownership of more complex customer enquiries and challenging interactions

 - Investigate issues, problem-solve and find practical solutions

 - Provide accurate, timely and high-quality information

 - Build deep knowledge of Netwealth’s products, services, processes and platform

 - Work closely with teams across Customer Operations, Sales, Product, Technology and Risk & Compliance

 - Build strong relationships with clients, advisers and external providers

 - Share your knowledge and experience with the team as the new Adelaide pod grows

 - Help create a customer experience that feels knowledgeable, human and genuinely helpful.



The underlying role requires strong product knowledge, attention to detail, problem-solving, professional communication and the ability to manage complex or challenging customer interactions. 



What we’re looking for

Because this is a Senior opportunity, we’re looking for someone who already has a strong grounding in financial services and can bring confidence and experience to a new team.

You’ll bring:

 - Strong experience in financial services customer service or operations

 - Knowledge of superannuation, investments, wealth management or platform administration

 - Confidence handling complex enquiries and working through problems to find the right solution

 - The ability to quickly learn and apply detailed product and process knowledge

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills

 - Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities

 - A calm, professional and empathetic approach when conversations become challenging

 - A natural willingness to share knowledge and support others

 - Curiosity, initiative and a genuine desire to keep learning and improving.

 - RG146 accreditation, or a willingness to obtain it, would be advantageous.
   
   

Why this opportunity is a little different 

There’s something pretty exciting about joining a team when it’s just getting started.

You won’t simply be joining the Adelaide pod. You’ll be part of its story from the beginning.

You’ll have the opportunity to bring your experience, help establish a strong team culture and grow alongside a business that values people who are Collaborative, Agile, Genuine, Optimistic, Curious and Courageous.

We’re looking for someone who wants to roll up their sleeves, get involved and help us create something great in Adelaide.

We’d love to hear from you!



Life At Netwealth

At Netwealth, we believe a fulfilling career is built on growth, balance, and belonging. Our people are our greatest strength, and we’re committed to supporting you at every stage of life because when you thrive, so do we.

We're proud to be recognised as one of Australia's top 5 companies for Career Development (endorsed by WORK180).  From further education and diverse training opportunities to strong support for internal mobility.  Your career can grow here.

Our flexible hybrid model supports balance, with just 4 days in the office each fortnight. When you’re in, you’ll enjoy working from one of our modern, thoughtfully designed spaces across Australia – including our state-of-the-art Melbourne CBD office. All locations feature contemporary facilities to make your day comfortable, and in Melbourne, you’ll also enjoy perks like end-of-trip amenities and daily breakfast to make your commute easier.

We offer benefits designed for your wellbeing and personal development, including;

 - Family-friendly support: Paid parental leave and a fully funded school holiday program

 - Wellness perks:  CU Health (virtual healthcare), income protection, flu shots, wellness weeks, retail discounts and financial wellbeing services

 - A vibrant culture:  social events, trivia nights, and corporate sports

 - Employee Resource Groups:  LGBTQIA+, DAWN (Development and Accelerating Women at Netwealth), Culture Group and Carers Group

 - Community Impact:  Paid volunteering and our Netwealth Impact Group

We're proud of our inclusive and diverse workforce and encourage everyone to bring their genuine selves to work. It's one of our core values.  We're committed to equity and inclusion through our gender equality, disability, LGBTQIA+, wellbeing and cultural initiatives.  And we're certified by WORK180, Family Friendly Workplaces and Great Places to Work.

If you're excited by the opportunity but don't meet every requirements, we still encourage you to apply.  Research shows people often hesitate unless they tick every box.  We value potential and passion just as much.

Need adjustments during the recruitment process?  Contact us at talent@netwealth.com.au

Apply now and help us shape a brighter financial future!

Campfire is an AI-native ERP built for mid-sized and enterprise companies. We help finance and accounting teams replace spreadsheets, manual reconciliations, and disconnected systems with one modern platform.

We’re backed by Y Combinator and have offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. We’ve raised more than $100 million, including a $35 million Series A led by Accel.

About the Role

We're looking for a strategic, well-connected partnerships leader to build our PE partnerships function from the ground up. You'll design and run a scalable program that engages PE firms and PE-backed companies. You'll work closely with our Head of PE & VC Practice, who will support you as you build the function.

The ideal candidate has already wokred in a PE Partner role, ideally at a technology startup. Experience selling or partnering around Office of the CFO technology is a strong plus.

What You'll Do

 - Build senior relationships with Private Equity Firms

 - Create partnership programs that deliver value to both sides, including customer introductions, portfolio company engagement, co-marketing, thought leadership, and strategic intelligence.

 - Serve as the main point of contact for PE partners, with a clear and consistent story for why they should work with us.

 - Build repeatable ways to source and manage opportunities from PE partners, including referral processes, partner enablement, reporting, and feedback loops.

 - Develop executive relationship plans for priority firms, and bring in senior leadership where it will strengthen the partnership.

 - Host and run our own PE events, and represent the company at industry events, portfolio company forums, and ecosystem gatherings.

 - Track market trends, and investment activity to spot strategic opportunities and inform internal decisions.

What You'll Bring

 - 3–7 years of experience in partnerships, business development, Private Equity , startup ecosystems, strategic alliances, or a related commercial role.

 - Proven experience in PE partnerships role, function, or program

 - Established relationships and credibility with PE firms

 - A track record of partnerships that delivered measurable business results.

 - Strong executive presence and the ability to earn trust with senior external partners and internal stakeholders.

 - Excellent communication, negotiation, and relationship management skills.

 - Data-driven judgment, including the ability to define KPIs and clearly report on partnership performance and impact.

 - Comfort working in a fast-moving environment.

 - A collaborative, low-ego approach: you're happy to roll up your sleeves, work across teams, and learn from our Head of PE & VC Practice.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience in B2B SaaS, enterprise technology, fintech, AI, cloud, cybersecurity, developer tools, or another high-growth technology category. Experience with Office of the CFO technology is strongly preferred.

 - Experience building partner referral, co-selling, or ecosystem programs.

jobs.title: Heavy Equipment Operator
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

HEAVY EQUIPMENT OPERATOR

The Heavy Equipment Operator is a skilled operator responsible for the safe, efficient operation of heavy earthmoving and material-handling equipment that supports Starship production, site development, and infrastructure work. This role runs excavators, loaders, dozers, graders, backhoes, and related machines to move materials, shape grades, and position components while production continues around the work. Operators work directly with engineers and technicians to inspect equipment, perform preventive maintenance, and catch issues before they stop the job. Success depends on precise control, strict safety compliance, and the ability to adapt as priorities change on a fast-moving site.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Operate heavy equipment in compliance with the company operating safety policies and procedures

• Conduct routine equipment inspections and preventative maintenance on equipment

• Move and position raw materials and finished components with use of material moving equipment

• Support inspection and maintenance of excavators, backhoe, bulldozers, graders, or loaders

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate

• 2+ years of professional experience working hands-on with heavy equipment, heavy equipment operations and/or production maintenance

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Valid CDL

• Experience installing civil infrastructure projects such as underground utilities

• Experience working with excavators, loaders, motor graders, dozers, or trenchers

• Experience performing area, volume and grade calculations in the field

• Able to adapt to constantly changing work assignments and fast-paced work environment

• Excellent concentration and attention to detail with outstanding work efficiency and accuracy

• Work in compliance with the applicable SpaceX and industry standards and regulations

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be available to work all shifts, overtime, and weekends as needed

• Must be able to climb ladders and work in tight spaces

• Required to exert physical effort in handling objects up to 50 pounds

• Required to be exposed to physical environment which involves dirt, odors, noise, weather extremes or similar elements most of the work day

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

jobs.title: Senior Space Avionics Hardware Development Engineer
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As a Senior Space Avionics Hardware Development Engineer at Varda, you will design and deliver flight-critical electrical hardware for our satellite bus, reentry vehicle, and customer payloads — owning your hardware domain from schematic capture through flight qualification. You will define subsystem requirements based on high level mission and company objectives, design to those requirements, and ensure the system as manufactured meets those requirements. In addition to designing and building electrical hardware, you will define its safe operating criteria and support our mission operations team on the risk tradeoffs of operating near the bounds of those criteria.

At Varda, we believe that the trip to space and back is the easiest trip our hardware takes. We stress our components above and beyond the levels it should expect to see in flight and investigate our failures thoroughly.

Responsibilities

• PCB level electronics design at all lifecycle stages, from schematic capture, to layout, to design validation, fabrication/assembly, and manufacturing test.

• Support avionics architecture trade studies, analyses, performance characterization and specification, device selection, and roadmap direction

• Avionics subject matter expert for satellite, reentry vehicle, and payload hardware. Providing support to those using your products, namely the Varda GNC, pharmaceutical, mission operations, and integration teams.

• Actively collaborate with cross functional teams such as flight software, thermal, GNC, and structures to determine across vehicle system impacts of design decisions.

• Ownership of product acceptance and qualification testing for space environments (Thermal, Vibe, Shock, TVAC, and EMI) with support from the Avionics Test team.

• Provide direction on system-level integration test plans to verify your hardware performs as expected at the vehicle level.

• Perform root cause analysis on test failures and implement holistic mitigation strategies for flight risks.

• Mentor junior engineers on their projects, challenges, and design methodologies setting a high bar for the future leaders of Varda.

Basic Qualifications

• B.S. in Electrical or Computer Engineering or related engineering discipline.

• 5+ years of direct experience designing electronics hardware - schematic capture, PCB layout, board bring-up, and environmental qualification - for aerospace, automotive, or other high-reliability industries.

• Demonstrated experience contributing to complex electronics systems from design to production/deployment.

• Advanced PCB design expertise, knowledge of high speed signal integrity, power and grounding, electromagnetic compatibility.

• Experience taking complex PCB designs through fabrication and assembly.

• Expert user of Altium and/or KiCad EDA suites.

• Strong hands-on lab experience with electronic test equipment including oscilloscopes, function generators, benchtop digital multimeters, and power supplies.

• Experience programming in Python, MATLAB, or another scripting/data analysis language.

• Demonstrated experience implementing the hardware layer of numerous on-board and over-harness communication protocols such as SPI, RS-422, and 1000BASE-T.

• Experience designing analog/digital filtering and mixed-signal circuits.

• Power electronics design experience including load switches and switch mode DC:DC converters.

Preferred Skills & Experience

• Industry leading electronic circuit design and analysis skills.

• Strong supporting general knowledge in physics, math, and chemistry fundamentals for designing electronics that experience unique environments.

• Understanding of aerospace sensor and actuator technologies including: RTDs, pressure transducers, brushless motors, solenoid valves, thermocouples, stepper motors, and rotary/linear Encoders.

Pay Range

• Salary range: $140,333 - $202,703/per year

• This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA

• Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance

• You will be eligible for long-term incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

ITAR Requirements

Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.

“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).

E-Verify Statement

Varda Space Industries, Inc. participates in the U.S. Department of Homeland Security E-Verify program. The E-Verify program is an Internet-based employment eligibility verification system operated by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. Learn more about the E-Verify program.

E-Verify Notice                                                               Right To Work Notice

Candidates and employees are always evaluated based on merit, qualifications, and performance. We will never discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, martial status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.

As a Principal Space Avionics Hardware Engineer at Varda, you will be the architect and designer of flight critical electrical hardware for our satellite bus, reentry vehicle, and customer payloads. Some examples include our flight computers, satellite power systems, sensors for navigation and monitoring pharmaceutical manufacturing. You will define subsystem requirements based on high level mission and company objectives, design to those requirements, and ensure the system as manufactured meets those requirements. In addition to designing and building electrical hardware, you will define its safe operating criteria and support our mission operations team on the risk tradeoffs of operating near the bounds of those criteria.

At Varda, we believe that the trip to space and back is the easiest trip our hardware takes. We stress our components above and beyond the levels it should expect to see in flight and investigate our failures thoroughly.

Responsibilities

• PCB level electronics design at all lifecycle stages, from schematic capture, to layout, to design validation, fabrication/assembly, and manufacturing test.

• Contribute to avionics architecture and system design for next-generation vehicles and hardware block upgrades to existing vehicles.

• Help define standards, processes and procedures to enable exemplary electrical engineering at Varda.

• Distilling high level company or mission objectives into requirements, designs, and developmental milestones for your subsystems.

• Avionics subject matter expert for satellite, reentry vehicle, and payload hardware. Providing support to those using your products, namely the Varda GNC, pharmaceutical, mission operations, and integration teams.

• Ownership of product acceptance and qualification testing for space environments (Thermal, Vibe, Shock, TVAC, and EMI) with support from the Avionics Test team.

• Provide direction on system-level integration test plans to verify your hardware performs as expected at the vehicle level.

• Perform root cause analysis on test failures and implement holistic mitigation strategies for flight risks.

• Mentor junior engineers on their projects, challenges, and design methodologies setting a high bar for the future leaders of Varda.

Basic Qualifications

• B.S. in Electrical or Computer Engineering or related engineering discipline.

• 8+ years of direct experience designing electronics hardware - schematic capture, PCB layout, board bring-up, and environmental qualification - for aerospace, automotive, or other high-reliability industries.

jobs.title: Research Intern
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/ and Clay Bavor https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.

Sierra’s Applied Research team works to make the models behind our agents better, faster, and cheaper across many kinds of tasks. Our work covers post-training open-weight models for specialized capabilities, new approaches to voice AI, and the benchmarks the field uses to measure agents, including τ-bench.

As an Applied Research Intern, you’ll join the team for a research project, working with a mentor, you’ll pick a problem that matters to how AI agents perform in the real world, run rigorous experiments, and potentially write up what you find for a top venue. If you want your research to reach both the research community and production agents used by millions of people, come do it at Sierra.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own a research project from start to finish, from framing the question and running experiments to writing and submitting a paper.

 - Push agent evaluation forward, for example by extending τ-bench to new domains, modalities, or long-horizon tasks, or by building new ways to measure reliability and consistency.

 - Study how agents reason, use tools, and follow policies over multi-turn conversations, and find out where and why they fail.

 - Explore post-training methods such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to improve agent behavior, and measure the gains rigorously.

 - Work with large-scale, proprietary datasets of text and audio interactions to find research questions grounded in real customer problems.

 - Work with researchers and engineers across Sierra, and where it makes sense, turn your findings into improvements in production.


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field.

 - A research track record, such as first-author publications or submissions at venues like NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, Interspeech or ICASSP.

 - Strong experimental skills: you design clean experiments, build careful baselines, and are honest about what the results do and do not show.

 - Fluency in Python and modern ML tooling (for example, PyTorch, and LLM inference and training stacks).

 - High agency and a builder’s mindset. You’ll work across the stack to get an experiment running.

 - Clear, direct communication, both in writing and when presenting research.


EVEN BETTER

 - Research experience with LLM agents, tool use, or multi-turn dialogue.

 - Experience designing benchmarks or evaluations, especially ones tied to real-world outcomes.

 - Experience with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or long-horizon optimization.

 - Experience with speech, voice, or multimodal models.

 - Open-source contributions to ML research code or benchmarks.


INTERN QUALIFICATIONS

 - The internship is open to students currently enrolled in a PhD program.

 - Duration and start dates are flexible. Interns are embedded with the Applied Research team and work under the guidance of a mentor.

 - The internship is based in our San Francisco office. We are in person Monday through Thursday.


OUR VALUES

 - Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

 - Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

 - Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

 - Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

 - Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements.


WHAT WE OFFER

We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees:

 - Flexible (unlimited) paid time off

 - Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family

 - Life insurance and disability benefits

 - Retirement plan dependent on country of employment

 - Parental leave

 - Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

 - Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized 

 - Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most

 - Free alphorn lessons

These benefits are further detailed in Sierra's policies, may vary by region, and are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefits plans. Eligible full-time employees can participate in Sierra's equity plans subject to the terms of the applicable plans and policies.


BE YOU, WITH US

We're working to bring the transformative power of AI to every organization in the world. To do so, it is important to us that the diversity of our employees represents the diversity of our customers. We believe that our work and culture are better when we encourage, support, and respect different skills and experiences represented within our team. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. We strive to evaluate all applicants consistently without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

jobs.title: Systems Engineer II – Systems
jobs.description:
Voyager is an innovative defense, national security and space technology company committed to advancing and delivering transformative, mission-critical solutions. We tackle the most complex challenges to unlock new frontiers for human progress, fortify national security, and protect critical assets to lead in the race for technological and operational superiority from ground to space.

Forge the Future: Join Voyager Technologies

The future belongs to those who build it. At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart.

You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Join a culture where innovation thrives, curiosity is rewarded, and impact is real. We’re a company of doers, thinkers and builders, united by purpose and grounded in reality.

If you want to put your skills to work where the stakes are real and the mission is bigger than any one person, forge the future with Voyager.

The Systems Engineer II – Systems position for Voyager – Strategic Systems supports requirements development, system verification activities, risk management, and MBSE efforts on MDA-aligned missile defense programs. This role focuses on executing defined systems engineering tasks under the guidance of senior engineers while developing a strong foundation in system-level thinking, technical documentation, and cross-functional collaboration.

The position reports to the Systems Engineering Manager and is part of the Strategic Systems Engineering Department based in Folsom, CA. This role can also be based in Reno, NV.

In this role, the essential functions are:

• Support development and maintenance of system, subsystem, and interface requirements; assist with traceability and compliance efforts

• Assist in development of system-level verification plans, procedures, and compliance matrices

• Support execution of system-level verification activities (e.g., reviews, inspections, and tests)

• Contribute to risk identification, documentation, and tracking; assist in developing mitigation strategies

• Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams including propulsion, software, hardware, test, GNC, quality, and safety

• Support communication of requirements, verification status, and technical issues with internal teams and stakeholders

• Assist in development and maintenance of Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) artifacts using SysML and Cameo/MagicDraw

• Participate in configuration management and change control processes

• Contribute to preparation for and participation in technical reviews (e.g., SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR)

• Support technical planning activities, including task tracking and status reporting

If your experience aligns with our basic qualifications and you are inspired by our mission, we’d like to connect. If you don’t see the right role right now, Join Our Talent Community and stay connected as we continue to build what’s next.

• Bachelor’s Degree in systems engineering, aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, or related STEM field from an accredited college/university. Master’s degree may substitute for 1 year of experience

• 2 to 4 years of systems engineering experience in DoD, aerospace, or related engineering programs

• Experience supporting requirements development, verification activities, or risk management

• Experience working in cross-functional engineering teams

• Familiarity with requirements management tools such as DOORS (or equivalent), SysML diagrams (e.g., block definition, activity, sequence), and MBSE tools such as Cameo Systems Modeler (MagicDraw)

• Familiarity with systems engineering lifecycle principles (e.g., INCOSE SE Handbook, MIL-STD-499, EIA-632)

• Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to support technical risk assessments and documentation

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Visio)

• Self-motivated with a willingness to learn, grow, and contribute in a team-oriented environment

Preferred Qualifications:

• Familiarity with Missile Defense Agency (MDA) processes or similar DoD program environments

• Exposure to technical reviews (e.g., SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR)

• Basic understanding of system architecture frameworks (e.g., DoDAF)

• Demonstrated strong work ethic, attention to detail, and commitment to mission success

Travel, Physical and/or Government Mandated Requirements:

• Travel up to approximately 10%

• U.S. Citizenship required due to federal contract eligibility

• Must have or be able to obtain and maintain an active DoD Secret Clearance

• Must comply with ITAR regulations

The good faith base salary range for this role is $82,460 – $128,000 at the time of this posting. Where you fall within the range depends on your experience, skills, and location. This range reflects base salary only and does not include benefits or bonus/incentive. This range may be adjusted in the future.

This position is incentive plan eligible.

Voyager offers a highly competitive total compensation package designed to support the well-being, growth, and success of our employees. Employees benefit from a flexible and comprehensive rewards program that supports both professional and personal well-being.

• Flexible Time Off (FTO), empowering employees to take the time they need to recharge and maintain a healthy work-life balance

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and their families, with a significant portion of premiums covered by the company and many benefits paid at 100% for employees

• Flexible, affordable gym memberships with 12,700+ options nationwide including 24 Hour Fitness, EoS Fitness, Crunch Fitness, Anytime Fitness, Blink Fitness, Chuze Fitness and more! No long-term contracts and FREE on-demand workout videos before you enroll

• 401(k) retirement plan with a company match of up to 4% to help you build long-term financial security

• Company wellness programs that support physical and mental well-being

• Additional voluntary benefits and employee support resources

• The opportunity to work alongside a highly talented team in an innovative, mission driven environment

Voyager is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by law.

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) (22 CFR Parts 120–130) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) (15 CFR Parts 730–774), applicants for this position must be a U.S. Person: a US Citizen, a lawful permanent resident of the U.S., or a protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. § 1324b(a)(3). Applicants must be eligible to obtain any required export authorizations from the U.S. Department of State or the U.S. Department of Commerce.

jobs.title: Patient Care Technician - I Medical Unit - FT - Days
jobs.description:
Position Objective:

Contributes to the provision of high-quality, cost-effective health care through the direct care of patients and in collaboration with other members of the health care team. Understands self-motivation in performing basic nursing care. Participates in the team nursing concept, completing tasks as delegated by the assigned nurse.

May be trained to insert IV’s on certain shifts/units.  Validation of training and skill will be documented, upon successful completion.

Essential Job Duties:

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions

• Provides direct care to patients with special attention to personal hygiene in daily morning and bedtime care and comfort. Initiates and maintains all types of safety measures and comfort care to patients.

• Assists with admission of patients by greeting and performing initial weight measurement, vital signs, disrobing as necessary and orientation of patient to room and equipment.

• Prioritizes discharge of patients by assisting with dressing, gathering belongings and transport if necessary to lobby; removes equipment and supplies from room for environmental staff cleaning.

• Participates in patient care, vital signs, intake and output and other data collection and records according to policy and procedure; obtains specimens as requested using approved procedure. Assists patients with mobilization and/or positioning as ordered by physician or unit protocol.

• Recognizes and reports pain, patient complaint or obvious change in patient condition to assigned nurse.

• Participates in the orientation of new staff acting as mentor when necessary and requested.

• Transports medications, as necessary during the usual course of transporting patients within the institution, in keeping with policy and procedure regarding medication security. Ensures that medication is delivered to persons authorized to handle medication according to AAMC policy.

• Maintains adequate levels of supplies and equipment on the unit.

• Transports patients in accordance with established safety policies.

• Processes written medical staff orders in accordance with established policy and procedure; communicating STAT or urgent orders to the care provider.

Educational/Experience Requirements:

• High School Diploma or GED

• One year of experience as a CNA in acute care setting preferred.

• If serving as a bilingual/multilingual interpreter, certification in Medical Interpretation is required to perform the duties of a qualified interpreter

Required License/Certifications:

• Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA)

• American Heart Association HealthCare Provider BLS

Additional Requirements by Department:

• STABLE: Pediatric Unit, Postpartum Care Unit, Neonatal Intensive Care Unit, and Labor and Delivery Unit within 6 months of hire

Working Conditions, Equipment, Physical Demands:

There is a reasonable expectation that employees in this position will be exposed to blood-borne pathogens.

Physical Demands –

Heavy work. Exerting up to 100 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 50 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 20 pounds of force constantly to move objects.

The physical demands and work environment that have been described are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act.

The above job description is an overview of the functions and requirements for this position.  This document is not intended to be an exhaustive list encompassing every duty and requirement of this position; your supervisor may assign other duties as deemed necessary.

Pay Range

$20.14—$23.75 USD

jobs.title: Financial Analyst (Risk Management & Internal Controls)
jobs.description:
White Pine Innovations is part of the Seneca Nation Group (SNG) portfolio of companies. SNG is Seneca Holdings’ federal government contracting business that meets mission-critical needs of federal civilian, defense, and intelligence community customers. Our portfolio comprises multiple subsidiaries that participate in the Small Business Administration 8(a) program. To learn more about SNG, visit the website and follow us on LinkedIn.

Our team of talented individuals is what makes us successful. To support our team, we provide a balanced mix of benefits and programs. Your total rewards package includes competitive pay, benefits, and perks, flexible work-life balance, professional development opportunities, and performance and recognition programs. We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life, and disability, voluntary benefit programs (critical illness, hospital, and accident), health savings and flexible spending accounts, and retirement 401K plan. One of our fundamental principles is to offer competitive health and welfare benefits to our team members, providing coverage and care for you and your family. Full-time employees working at least 30 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in our benefits and paid leave programs.  We pride ourselves on our collaborative work environment and culture, which embraces our mission of providing financial and non-financial benefits back to the members of the Seneca Nation.

White Pine Innovations is seeking a highly skilled and experienced Financial Analyst to join our dynamic team, with a specific focus on Audit and Risk Management Internal Control (RMIC) support. This role plays a crucial part in ensuring the integrity of our financial processes and controls, as well as facilitating successful audits and risk management efforts.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Collaborate within the Accounting Branch in a supporting role to help monitor the status of audit responses, address auditor inquiries, and furnish the required documentation.

• Assist in the implementation of audit recommendations and improvements to internal controls.

• Contribute to the development and maintenance of robust internal controls and risk management practices.

• Monitor and evaluate financial processes and controls to identify areas for improvement and risk mitigation.

• Support the RMIC team in conducting risk assessments and developing mitigation strategies.

• Identify opportunities for process improvements related to financial controls, reporting, and audit readiness.

• Work with stakeholders to implement enhancements and streamline financial processes.

• Prepare and present periodic reports to management regarding audit findings and RMIC initiatives.

Basic Qualifications:

• Due to the nature of the contract, US. citizenship is required.

• Active Public Trust clearance.

• BS or BA in a relevant field such as finance or accounting. Five years of experience in lieu of a degree could be considered.

• Basic knowledge of accounting principles, internal controls, and auditing standards.

• Strong attention to detail and the ability to work independently and in a team.

• Experience prioritizing tasks, working on multiple assignments, and managing ambiguity.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities for effective collaboration with cross-functional teams.

• Ability to adapt to changing priorities and work independently in a fast-paced environment.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint, as well as Internet research tools.

Desired Skills:

• CPA or relevant professional certification.

• Experience with DoD Audit readiness/response procedures and DoD’s Risk Management and Internal Controls (RMIC) Program.

• 1-3+ years of experience in Audit readiness, to include Financial Improvement Audit Readiness (FIAR), and OMB Circular A-123.

• 1-3+ years of experience performing process improvement, gap analysis, SOP development, or Policy development.

• 1-3+ years of experience performing financial statement audits and/or auditability assessments.

• Familiarity with U.S. government General Ledger

• “Big 4” experience.

Equal Opportunity Statement:
Seneca Holdings provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex/gender, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, marital status, genetic information and/or predisposing genetic characteristics, victim of domestic violence status, veteran status, or other protected class status. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including, but not limited to, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leave of absence, compensation and training. The Company also prohibits retaliation against any employee who exercises his or her rights under applicable anti-discrimination laws. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Company does give hiring preference to Seneca or Native individuals. Veterans with expertise in these areas are highly encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Senior Success Lead, Public Sector
jobs.description:
Datavant is the data collaboration platform trusted for healthcare. Guided by our mission to make the world’s health data secure, accessible and actionable, we provide critical data solutions for organizations across the healthcare ecosystem - including providers, health plans, researchers, and life sciences companies. From fulfilling a single patient’s request for their medical records to powering the AI revolution in healthcare, Datavanters are building the future of how data is connected and used to improve health.

By joining Datavant today, you’re stepping onto a driven and highly collaborative team that is passionate about creating transformative change in healthcare.

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for an experienced relationship pro with deep experience in government and public sector engagement, who excels in fast-paced environments and is eager to drive impact as part of our Strategic Engagement  team.  Strategic Engagement  is the value organization of Datavant Life Sciences. We are accountable for driving meaningful, measurable outcomes for our customers by aligning our products and services with their strategic objectives—maximizing value, accelerating time to impact, and fostering long-term, expansive relationships.  As such, we need an experienced relationship management individual who can drive success for our customers.

This role includes responsibilities for commercial outcomes (e.g., value realization, customer satisfaction, renewals, etc.) and post-sale activities (e.g., strategic engagement leadership, delivery, adoption, advocacy, retention, etc.).

What You Will Do

• Own engagement management and value management for a dedicated account portfolio of up to 5 accounts in our government practice, with a special focus on end-to-end accelerating value within your portfolio.

• Develop a deep understanding of how our current government and government channel partner accounts that are using data to achieve strategic objectives through a variety of engagement techniques (e.g. frequent engagement-focused meetings, workshops, quarterly business reviews, etc.). Innovate ideas on how to support our partners in achieving success as they would define it.

• Lead with curiosity and dive deep into learning and understanding the goals and strategies of our customers and how our solutions and products support those goals.

• Excel in complex program management, often involving multiple partners and contractors, and decision-making, balancing thoughtful analysis with speed to execution, appropriately prioritizing, and knowing when and how to escalate complex edge cases effectively.

• Drive long-term customer value by boosting product adoption, strengthening satisfaction and health, and building trusted, lasting relationships.

• Thrive in a fast-paced, continuous improvement environment, embracing gray areas and ambiguity, while seeking to drive clarity and scalability for your customers and the business.

• Work effectively with your cross-functional partners - surfacing insights that influence product and sales strategies across account teams for your portfolio accounts.

• Take a self-service-first approach to problem solving and navigating questions internally and externally.

• Be a proven communicator and presenter with a commitment to maintaining good internal and external relationships through passion, empathy, and hard work.

• Help create a company-wide culture of customer-centricity.

What You Need to Succeed

• 7+ years experience in healthcare technology and customer facing roles (required)

• 4+ years experience in the federal government or with government contractors and government adjacent organizations (required)

• Experienced strategic program and project manager focused on connecting the dots thinking that puts client value at the center of everything

• Proven ability to build deep, trust-based relationships with customer stakeholders

• Skilled at expanding relationships beyond direct contacts through rapport-building

• Demonstrated ownership of complex, high-value customer accounts

• Strategic thinker who connects cross-customer trends to shape value propositions

• Effective and empathetic internal and external communication

What Helps You Stand Out

• Previous experiencing working in one or more of the following areas (preferred): Experience working within a government agency or government-adjacent organization, RWD health analytic companies, CROs, or systems integrators in the healthcare sector Experience with clinical data, RWD/RWE, patient consent, and/or HIPAA privacy requirements Application of RWD and RWE in the pharmaceutical and life sciences space Understanding of drug development and/or clinical trials Experience with technology in multiple federal health agencies/departments including but not limited to HHS, NIH, FDA, CMS, ARPA-H, CDC, AHRQ, SAMHSA, HRSA, ASPE, ONC/ASTP, VHA, DHA, DARPA, etc. Experience working with program officers, CORs, and senior government stakeholders as clients, including building trusted relationships with agency leadership.

jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. TOOLING DESIGNER, INJECTION MOLDING

SpaceX is leveraging its experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to 10M+ users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact. As we continue to upgrade and expand the constellation, we’re looking for best-in-class engineers to join the team.

As part of the materials engineering team, you will provide expertise and capabilities to developing processes for the production of plastic injection molds. You will make an impact on SpaceX’s Starlink product components alongside a strong group of mechanical and process engineers. The goal of the team is to develop new manufacturing methods, commission equipment and qualify processes to be introduced into production.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Own parting line development and surfacing of in-house molds and components

• Responsible for all design for manufacturability (DFM) studies on plastic injection molded components

• Own and manage the feasibility and surfacing of critical mold components

• Interpret mold filling simulations and cooling analyses to drive feasibility and tool design

• Design tools to be manufactured in-house

• Support external tool designs and attend mold trials at vendor shops

• Ensure designs are safe, effective, and manufacturable

• 5+ years of professional experience as a designer

• Experience with hot runner systems

• Experience with multi-shot, compression and other tooling

• Knowledge of drafting practices and principles

TOOLING ENGINEER, PLASTIC INJECTION MOLDING (STARLINK)

jobs.title: Senior Mechanical Engineer
jobs.description:
Xona is the navigational intelligence company bringing real-time, centimeter-level certainty to any device, anywhere on Earth.



With Pulsar – the world’s most advanced PNT satellite infrastructure in Low Earth Orbit – Xona will offer a future-proof, backwards-compatible global positioning system optimized for absolute precision, superior power, and robust protection.



Role Overview

We’re looking for a Senior Mechanical Engineer who can take a complex mechanical problem, define a practical approach, and deliver reliable hardware. You will own spacecraft subsystems and critical equipment from early requirements and trade studies through design, build, qualification, and production support.

Projects may include primary structure, deployable mechanisms, launch vehicle interfaces, solar arrays, machined and sheet metal brackets, electronics enclosures, precision mounts, and high-criticality mechanical ground support equipment (GSE). Your assignments will evolve with the needs of the spacecraft and the team.

You will work with substantial autonomy, make sound decisions with incomplete information, and help the team resolve its most challenging mechanical issues. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with technical leadership and mentoring responsibilities.

What you will do

 - Own complex mechanical subsystems from concept through qualification and production, establishing requirements, interfaces, verification plans, and realistic delivery schedules.

 - Lead mechanical trade studies and contribute to spacecraft layouts and architecture, balancing load paths, packaging, thermal interfaces, reliability, cost, manufacturability, and integration needs.

 - Design flight hardware and critical GSE; release CAD, drawings, bills of materials, and interface definitions with clear GD&T, tolerance analysis, and configuration control.

 - Use first-principles calculations and structural FEA to substantiate designs. Partner with structural and thermal specialists to define loads, boundary conditions, margins, and verification needs.

 - Build prototypes, work directly with hardware, and develop fixtures and functional tests to retire risks. Own qualification of assigned hardware and occasionally support spacecraft vibration and TVAC campaigns.

 - Lead resolution of build, integration, test, and production anomalies: contain the issue, investigate root cause, implement corrective action, and verify the fix.

 - Own supplier technical execution, including requirements, design reviews, procurement coordination, inspection criteria, and resolution of manufacturing issues.

 - Coordinate across mechanical, thermal, electrical, payload, GNC, manufacturing, and integration and test teams. Identify risks early, communicate tradeoffs, and drive issues to closure.

 - Review designs, mentor engineers, and improve engineering practices while remaining directly responsible for delivering hardware.



Required qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related engineering field.

 - 7+ years of mechanical hardware development experience, with demonstrated responsibility for complex assemblies or subsystems in aerospace or another high-reliability field.

 - A record of independently taking hardware from requirements and concept through detailed design, build, and qualification or equivalent verification.

 - Strong mechanical fundamentals, including load paths, joints and fasteners, materials, thermal and optical properties, manufacturing processes, GD&T, and tolerance analysis.

 - Proficiency in 3D CAD and drawing release using SolidWorks or a comparable platform, with disciplined PDM and configuration management practices.

 - Ability to perform and critically assess structural calculations and FEA, understand modeling assumptions, and reconcile analysis with physical test results.

 - Hands-on experience assembling, inspecting, troubleshooting, and testing hardware, including resolving issues during integration or production.

 - Demonstrated judgment in technical tradeoffs, clear communication across disciplines, and experience guiding design reviews or mentoring other engineers.
   
   

Preferred qualifications

 - Experience with spacecraft hardware, launch environments, or other high-reliability hardware with demanding structural and environmental requirements.

 - Experience with deployment or separation mechanisms, precision assemblies, electronics packaging, or spacecraft handling and lifting equipment.

 - Experience supporting vibration, shock, or thermal vacuum (TVAC) testing and using test results to improve hardware.

 - Experience transitioning designs into repeatable production, resolving supplier issues, or improving assembly and inspection processes.

 - Experience leading subsystem architecture, managing complex supplier deliverables, or coordinating technical interfaces with launch providers or deployer vendors.

Experience in every hardware category listed above is not expected. We are interested in the depth of your engineering work, the hardware you have delivered, and your ability to apply that experience to new problems.

For U.S. Roles: To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States (i.e. Green Card holder), or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3). 



For U.K. Roles: To comply with U.K. regulations, this role requires Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) checks, and successful candidates must be eligible to obtain UK Security Clearance (SC).



For Canada Roles: Successful candidates must obtain and hold a security clearance at the reliability status level, and pass security assessment for the Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and ITAR.
