jobs.title: Construction Superintendent, Fluid/Mechanical - Memphis
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

CONSTRUCTION SUPERINTENDENT, FLUID/MECHANICAL

Most construction jobs manage someone else’s crew on someone else’s schedule, then end when the project does. This one does not.

SpaceX builds its own launch sites, factories, test stands, and AI superclusters — and it plans to keep building. The rockets, the chips, and the missions only matter if the ground under them is real. Construction is how that ground gets built, in-house and to a standard the company can actually use. The work does not dry up between jobs. There is a next site, and one after that. You lead the crew that builds them.

You own a self-performing team. Foremen run their people day to day. You run the foremen. You are in the dirt, walking the work, setting the bar, and clearing whatever is in the way. When someone is ready for more, you say so. When the standard slips, you deal with it.

Scope includes, but not limited to industrial HVAC, pipefitting, pipe welding, chilled water, cooling towers, chillers, condensers, CRAC and CRAH units, and setting that heavy mechanical equipment. It also includes all plumbing: domestic water, sanitary, drain-waste-vent, and floor drains. It includes all fire protection: sprinkler fitting, suppression, and pre-action. This is the work that moves heat, water, and fire protection through the building.

The team goes where the next site is — a pad, a factory, a supercluster, whatever has to exist before the rest of the company can move. Right now that is Memphis, TN / Southaven, MS. Then it is the next one. Per diem comes with the assignment.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Directly oversee foremen and, through them, a large self-perform fluid/mechanical crew installing industrial HVAC, pipe, chilled water, cooling towers, chillers, condensers, CRAC and CRAH units, plumbing, and fire protection, including pipe welding and setting heavy mechanical equipment

• Set clear expectations for safety, quality, schedule, and conduct, and hold foremen and crews accountable when those expectations are missed

• Remove roadblocks so crews can keep working: materials, access, sequencing, coordination with other trades, and decisions

• Recommend promotions, role changes, and corrective action based on performance

• Plan and run the night-shift assignment, including extended hours, as part of a 24/7 operation

• Keep fluid and mechanical installations on SpaceXSI’s quality and reliability standards, including code compliance and system integrity required for data center cooling and fire protection

• Track daily progress and maintain logs, red-line drawings, and as-built documentation for mechanical, plumbing, and fire-protection systems

• Build and hold an aggressive construction schedule, on time and within budget

• Champion SpaceXSI’s safety program and a zero-incident culture around pressure piping, hot work, rigging and setting heavy mechanical equipment, and work at heights

• Resolve on-site issues — material delays, technical conflicts, sequencing, and trade coordination — with attention to system integrity and code compliance

• Inspect work for compliance with local regulations, mechanical, plumbing, and fire-protection codes, safety protocols, and SpaceXSI quality standards

• Report progress, fluid/mechanical construction metrics, and risks to senior leadership

• Relocate with the mobile team as assignments change, starting in Memphis, TN / Southaven, MS

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate

• 3+ years leading fluid/mechanical construction teams, including supervision of foremen

• 3+ years of direct hands-on experience in fluid/mechanical installations, including industrial HVAC, pipefitting, chilled water, plumbing, or fire protection

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Experience leading large self-perform crews on industrial or mission-critical mechanical, piping, or fire-protection projects

• Direct hands-on experience on industrial processes or heavy mechanical projects

• Postsecondary diploma or degree in construction management, mechanical engineering, or a related field

• Track record on data centers, hyperscale facilities, or similar mission-critical mechanical construction

• Familiarity with Memphis-area building codes, IMC, IPC, NFPA 13, and industrial permitting

• Experience with Procore, AutoCAD, Bluebeam, MS Project, or similar tools on complex infrastructure work

• Strong grasp of mechanical critical path, sequencing, and coordination with electrical, structural, and civil trades through commissioning

• Understanding of data center cooling and fire-protection requirements, including chilled water, cooling towers, CRAC and CRAH units, and systems built for 24/7 operation

• History of leading diverse crews to a deadline without giving up collaboration or safety

• Working knowledge of lockout/tagout, hot work, pressure testing, and a record of building a safety culture on regulated sites

• Strong problem-solving and conflict resolution on technically complex mechanical, plumbing, and fire-protection work

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Teams, Project)

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Subject to pre-employment drug screening and random drug/alcohol testing, and pre-employment/post-employment background checks

• This role is part of the mobile construction team and you will be expected to travel to the assigned work project. Current work assignment is based in Memphis, TN / Southaven, MS. Future assignments will require relocation to other U.S. construction sites. Per diem is provided while on assignment

• Must be willing to work any shift, extended hours and/or holidays during assigned work assignment. This includes rotating shifts, nights and/or weekends. If you are assigned night shift, you will receive a shift differential for hours worked during off nominal hours

• Must be willing to work in industrial environments with exposure to noise, heavy equipment, excavations, and energized electrical systems. Must be able to lift 25 lbs or more and perform physically demanding tasks outdoors, indoors, in tight conditions, and/or at heights, with or without reasonable accommodation

SpaceXSI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

jobs.title: Commercial Sales Development Representative
jobs.description:
About Delinea:
Delinea is the identity security platform that continuously controls what AI agents, humans and machines can do and for how long. It extends privileged access management from the point of access to the moment of action, using just-in-time authorization to reduce standing privilege across on-premises, multi-cloud and short-lived infrastructure, without adding friction for legitimate users. Delinea provides visibility across every identity type, scores the risk each one carries, and preserves the context behind access decisions, making them auditable and defensible. It supports both static and ephemeral access, letting teams apply Zero Standing Privilege where risk demands it without replacing existing infrastructure.



Position Summary:

The Commercial Sales Development Representative (C-SDR) at Delinea is a full-time, hybrid, position based at our Boston location (100 Summer Street). As an entry-level position, this role serves as a vital connection between our Sales and Marketing teams, focusing on generating and qualifying leads to create business opportunities. The Commercial SDR is responsible for initiating communication with potential customers, understanding their needs, and setting the stage for a successful sales process.



What You’ll Do:

 1. Prospecting and Lead Generation: Proactively reach out to potential customers through phone (80%), email, and LinkedIn to identify and qualify new business opportunities.

 2. Lead Qualification: Process and qualify inbound leads to generate sales opportunities, ensuring alignment with Delinea's sales goals.

 3. Pipeline Development: Execute a minimum of 75+ outbound activities daily, including calls and emails, to build and maintain a strong pipeline of qualified leads.

 4. Research and Relationship Building: Conduct thorough research to gather account intelligence, identify key stakeholders, and build relationships with IT decision-makers.

 5. Collaboration: Partner closely with the Sales team to develop and refine go-to-market strategies, ensuring a seamless handoff of qualified leads.

 6. Learning and Development: Continuously enhance your knowledge of Delinea’s product offerings and the cybersecurity industry through internal e-learning platforms.

 7. Data Management: Keep accurate records of all sales activities in CRM tools (Salesforce) and Prospect Engagement systems (SalesLoft) to monitor progress and success.



Location:

 1. This position is hybrid in-office 3 days a week and based at Delinea's Boston office located at 100 Summer Street. Full time remote work or telecommuting is not available for this role.



What You’ll Bring:

 1. Educational Background: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.

 2. Communication Skills: Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to effectively engage with decision-makers.

 3. Drive and Motivation: A strong desire to learn and grow in a sales role, with a goal-oriented and data-driven mindset.

 4. Technological Proficiency: Basic understanding of CRM systems, with a preference for familiarity with Salesforce or similar platforms.



You’ll Stand Out If You Have:

 1. Industry Knowledge: Exposure to technology sales, customer service, or a related field through internships or work experience.

 2. Sales Techniques: Familiarity with sales approaches such as cold calling, personalized messaging, or pipeline management.

 3. Adaptability: An eagerness to quickly learn and apply new concepts, especially in a dynamic, technology-driven environment.



Why work at Delinea? 

 - We're passionate problem-solvers helping the world's largest organizations protect what matters most: their human and machine identities.

 - We invest in people who are smart, self-motivated, and collaborative.

 - What we offer in return is meaningful work, a culture of innovation and great career progression.



At Delinea, our core values are STRONG and guide our behaviors and success:

 - Spirited - We bring energy and passion to everything we do

 - Trust - We act with integrity and deliver on our commitments

 - Respect - We listen, value different perspectives, and work as one team

 - Ownership - We take initiative and follow through

 - Nimble - We adapt quickly in a fast-changing environment

 - Global - We embrace diverse people and ideas to drive better outcomes

We believe weaving these core values into our day-to-day actions, and our process for hiring, evaluating, and promoting employees, helps us cultivate a work environment that embraces collaboration and camaraderie.

We take care of our employees. We offer competitive salaries, a meaningful bonus program, and excellent benefits, including healthcare insurance, as well as pension/retirement matching, comprehensive life insurance, an employee assistance program, time off plans, and paid company holidays. 

Delinea is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type with regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Upon conditional offer of employment, candidates are required to complete comprehensive criminal background check, verification of education, and verification of employment, per employment policy. In addition, all publicly posted social media sites may be reviewed.

jobs.title: Equipment Maintenance Engineer
jobs.description:
About Harbinger

Harbinger is an American commercial electric vehicle (EV) company on a mission to transform an industry starving for innovation. Harbinger’s best-in-class team of EV, battery, and drivetrain experts have pooled their deep experience to bring a first-of-its-kind EV platform to support the growing demand for medium-duty EVs and Hybrids. Harbinger: Familiar Form, Revolutionary Foundation.

Role Overview

Harbinger Motors is expanding, and we are looking for an Equipment Maintenance Engineer to support our advanced EV manufacturing lines (Battery, General Assembly, EDU, Stator/Hairpin). This role ensures high equipment reliability, uptime, and performance across highly automated production systems. You will collaborate with Production, Process Engineering, Quality, and external suppliers to diagnose failures, implement improvements, and drive preventive and predictive maintenance strategies.

What You'll Do:

Equipment Reliability & Maintenance

• Perform advanced troubleshooting and resolve electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, hydraulic, and automation-related failures.

• Maximize uptime for critical equipment and meet key maintenance KPIs (MTBF, MTTR, OEE).

• Develop, execute, and continuously improve preventive and predictive maintenance plans (e.g., vibration analysis, thermography, and failure analysis).

• Conduct root-cause analyses (RCA, 5 Whys, Ishikawa) and implement robust corrective and preventive actions.

Automation & Controls

• Troubleshoot and program PLCs at a basic to intermediate level (Siemens/Allen-Bradley).

• Manage industrial communication networks, including Ethernet/IP, Profinet, CAN, and Modbus.

• Configure drives, servo motors, sensors, HMIs, and industrial safety systems.

• Interpret and update electrical schematics, P&IDs, and pneumatic diagrams.

Mechanical & Industrial Systems

• Maintain and optimize mechanical systems, including transmissions, actuators, bearings, alignments, torque specifications, vacuum systems, pumps, and chillers.

• Diagnose mechanical failures related to vibration, temperature, noise, or abnormal behavior.

• Replace, adjust, and evaluate wear and tear on critical machine components.

Projects & Continuous Improvement

• Lead improvement projects focused on efficiency, automation upgrades, safety, and downtime reduction.

• Collaborate with integrators, OEMs, and suppliers for troubleshooting and system upgrades.

• Document equipment modifications in accordance with quality standards (ISO 9001 and IATF 16949 preferred).

• Support engineering change processes (ECR/ECN).

Safety & Compliance

• Ensure compliance with OSHA, NFPA 70E, ISO standards, and machine-safety regulations (EN/ISO 12100, 13849).

• Participate in risk assessments, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures, safety audits, and 5S/6S activities.

• Implement engineering controls to proactively reduce operational risks.

Production Support

• Provide direct, hands-on support during critical equipment failures and production ramp-ups.

• Train and mentor maintenance technicians on advanced troubleshooting and repair methodologies.

• Ensure equipment consistently meets cycle time, quality, and performance requirements.

Who You Are:

Education

• Bachelor’s degree in Mechatronics, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.

Experience

• 2–5 years of experience in the maintenance of automated manufacturing equipment.

• Hands-on experience with automated assembly equipment, robotics, End-of-Line (EOL) testing, and servo-driven systems.

Technical Skills

• PLCs: Siemens TIA Portal, Allen-Bradley Studio 5000.

• Industrial Electrical Systems: 480VAC, 24VDC controls, and interpreting electrical schematics.

• Sensors: Inductive, optical, laser, pressure, temperature, and vision systems.

• Mechanical Systems: Pneumatics, hydraulics, alignments, torque, fittings, and tolerances.

• Software: Proficiency with CMMS software (MaintainX preferred).

• Documentation: Ability to read and interpret technical manuals fluently in English.

Soft Skills

• Strong sense of urgency and ownership over equipment performance.

• Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.

• Effective communication skills for working seamlessly with cross-functional teams.

• Ability to work effectively under pressure in time-critical manufacturing situations.

• Proactive mindset with a strong continuous-improvement mentality.

• Flexibility to work extended hours as production demands require.

Preferred Qualifications

Certifications:

• Siemens or Rockwell Automation (basic to intermediate)

• OSHA 10 or OSHA 30

• Six Sigma (Yellow or Green Belt)

• Predictive Maintenance (vibration analysis, thermography)

Additional Experience:

• Hands-on experience with robotics (Fanuc, ABB, or KUKA).

• Prior experience in automotive, electric vehicle (EV), electronics, or other high-automation environments.

Key Benefits & Perks:

• Comprehensive Health, Dental & Vision (HDV) – 100% employee covered

• Early-stage Stock Options

• Robust Retirement Savings (401k, HSA, FSA)

• Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) & Parental Leave

• Annual Vacation Bonus

• Wellness & Fertility Benefits

• Cell Phone Stipend

• Complimentary Meals & Stocked Kitchens

California Pay Range

$140,000—$180,000 USD

Equal Opportunity

Harbinger is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Harbinger is committed to ensuring that our hiring process is accessible for persons with disabilities. If you have a disability or limitation, such as those covered by the Americans with Disabilities Act, that requires accommodations to assist you in the search and application process, please email us at info@harbingermotors.com.

Candidate Data Privacy

Harbinger may collect, use and disclose your personal information or personal data (within the meaning of the applicable data protection laws) when you apply for employment and/or participate in our recruitment processes (“Candidate Personal Data”). This data includes contact, demographic, communications, educational, professional, employment, social media/website, network/device, recruiting system usage/interaction, security and preference information. Harbinger may use your Candidate Personal Data for the purposes of (i) tracking interactions with our recruiting system; (ii) carrying out, analyzing and improving our application and recruitment process, including assessing you and your application and conducting employment, background and reference checks; (iii) establishing an employment relationship or entering into an employment contract with you; (iv) complying with our legal, regulatory and corporate governance obligations; (v) recordkeeping; (vi) ensuring network and information security and preventing fraud; and (vii) as otherwise required or permitted by applicable law.

Harbinger may share your Candidate Personal Data with (i) internal personnel who have a need to know such information in order to perform their duties, including individuals on our HR, legal, and finance teams, and the team(s) with the position(s) for which you are applying; (ii) Harbinger affiliates; and (iii) Harbinger’s service providers, including providers of background checks, staffing services, and cloud services.

Harbinger may transfer or store internationally your Candidate Personal Data, including to or in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the European Union and in the cloud, and this data may be subject to the laws and accessible to the courts, law enforcement and national security authorities of such jurisdictions.

Please note that we are currently not accepting applications from third party application services. Any unsolicited resumes or candidate profiles submitted in response to our job posting shall be considered the property of Harbinger and are not subject to payment of referral or placement fees if any such candidate is later hired by Harbinger unless you have a signed written agreement in place with us which covers the applicable job posting.

jobs.description:

jobs.title: Ops Recruiter
jobs.description:
ABOUT MERCOR



Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.


ABOUT THE ROLE

As an Ops Recruiter at Mercor, you’ll own full-cycle hiring for critical roles across a variety of organizations, with a particular focus on our Delivery org. You will partner directly with General Managers and Account Leads to find high performing operators that will partner directly with the leading AI Labs in the world, playing an instrumental role in scaling one of the fastest-growing companies in the world. This is a true 0→1 motion, with an opportunity to lay the foundation for the future of recruiting at Mercor.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own full-cycle recruiting (sourcing → close) across a variety of organizations (such as marketing, finance, people ops, with a prominent focus on operations)

 - Partner with b to map out needs and implement continual process improvements

 - Build top-of-funnel using creative outbound, talent intelligence, and Mercor’s own product (structured screens, automated work samples, and calibrated rubrics)

 - Coach hiring managers and interviewers on structured interviewing, leveling, and decision hygiene

 - Operationalize hiring systems: track and optimize key funnel metrics (pass-through rates, time-in-stage, source yield)

 - Champion speed and quality: drive SLAs for same-day debriefs, fast offers, and strong candidate experience

 - Build brand: campaigns, referrals, and events that attract top engineers and operators

 - Represent Mercor externally, you’ll be a face of the brand for an exceptionally competitive talent market

 - Collaborate on dashboards, metrics, and process automation within Ashby and other recruiting systems

 - Refinement of technical recruiting motion as the Ops org shifts to hire more frequently from technical backgrounds
   
   


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience with full-cycle recruiting across IC and leadership roles

 - Proven ability to build and scale hiring systems, identify key metrics, and make data-driven decisions

 - High motor, outcome-oriented approach; Mercor is in hypergrowth, and hiring is viewed as a key strategic driver of that growth

 - Strong communication skills; able to work efficiently with General Managers, Account Leads, and internal leadership

 - Familiarity with a range of roles, emphasis on GTM, Strategy, Operations, ideally with some mastery of technical roles such as SWEs or FDEs

 - Confident representing the Mercor brand to top candidates

 - Familiarity with Ashby or ability to quickly adopt new tools and systems
   
   


NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience as a founding recruiter or early-stage startup builder

 - Interest in the human data / AGI space

 - Technical recruiting expertise - Mercor's business is trending in an increasingly technical perspective over time, and we are hiring a greater percentage of technical professionals into client facing operator roles
   
   


IDEAL QUALITIES

 - Agility / Adaptability - ability to move fast, pivot with business shifts, and maintain best-in-class outcomes

 - Operational Rigor - ability to bring order to an unstructured environment

 - Growth Mindset - You don’t need to be an expert on AI, but you do need to have a strong desire to learn and continue learning in a rapidly evolving, frontier industry

 - Commitment to the Outcome - Ownership mentality; will hold themselves accountable to an extremely high standard of work

 - Love for the Craft - we are building a zero to one motion; this hire will bring a low ego attitude to the table with a genuine love for building a best-in-class talent acquisition motion
   
   


BENEFITS

 - $15K relocation bonus (for moving to the Bay Area)

 - $10K housing bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

 - $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

 - Free Equinox membership

 - $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

 - $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

 - Health, Dental, Vision insurance

 - 401(k) with company match

jobs.title: Manager, Solar Engineering
jobs.description:
K2 is building the largest and highest-power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.

The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today's and tomorrow's massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.

With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.

The Role

Solar power isn’t a subsystem at K2, it’s the capability that makes everything else possible. Our arrays are what allow us to operate at power levels no satellite has ever sustained, across the most demanding orbits in the solar system. Getting that right, at scale, is one of the most consequential engineering challenges in the company.

As the Manager, Solar Engineering, you’ll own it entirely. From early-stage technology development and module innovation through design maturation, manufacturing, test, and on-orbit performance – the solar array program is yours to build and lead. You will grow a cross-functional organization spanning design, analysis, manufacturing, and integration, and set the technical direction and operational cadence needed to meet our most ambitious cost, schedule, and reliability targets.

The missions we’re building toward are unlike anything the industry has flown: extreme radiation environments, multi-year lifetimes, and production volumes that demand manufacturing infrastructure built for rate and not one-off heroics. This is a rare opportunity to define what world-class solar engineering looks like inside a vertically integrated space company, and to build the team and systems that make it real.

Responsibilities

• Build, scale, and lead the Solar Engineering organization across design, manufacturing, process, and automation disciplines

• Own the solar hardware technical baseline end-to-end: from array and module design through process qualification, tooling and automation infrastructure, and flight-ready production delivery

• Take hardware and mechanisms from conceptual design through qualification to on-orbit operations, including hands-on testing, analysis, and iterative design refinement

• Identify and invest in transformative technologies that unlock step-change improvements in rate, reliability, and unit economics

• Set the strategic direction for how solar hardware is designed and manufactured at scale, establishing the systems, processes, and standards that enable high-rate production

• Collaborate with a cross-functional team to establish product requirements, company processes, and best practices for hardware design and manufacturing

• Represent Solar Engineering at the executive level driving alignment on technical direction, risk, and program execution

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, aerospace, or other relevant engineering discipline

• 5+ years of experience with mechanical and/or electromechanical design and analysis in solar or electro-mechanical systems

• 1+ years of experience building and leading large, multi-disciplinary engineering teams including managing managers and developing senior ICs across multiple functional areas

• Demonstrated ability to own a complex engineering function end-to-end through major program phases, from development and design iteration through production ramp and sustained delivery

• Executive-level communication and stakeholder management skills

• Experience with CAD or FEA software packages

Nice to Have

• Direct experience leading solar array engineering for space applications, spanning design, module interconnect processes, module lamination, integrated PVA construction, and flight array integration

• Demonstrated background scaling a multi-disciplinary engineering organization from early-stage development to full-rate production in a high-reliability or aerospace environment

• Hands-on background in robotics, vision-guided assembly, or electromechanical controls for manufacturing applications

• Experience designing, building, and testing moving mechanical assemblies for aerospace applications (satellite mechanical systems, payloads, launch vehicles, propulsion systems, and/or aircraft structures and mechanisms)

• Experience with NASA-STD-5017, SMC-S-016, and GSFC-STD-7000 for the design and qualification of in-space Moving Mechanism Assemblies

• Experience with the practical application of GD&T

• Independent and self-motivated mindset, with strong organizational, written, and oral communication skills across disciplines

Compensation and Benefits:

• Base salary range for this role is $150,000 - $250,000 + equity in the company

• Salary and level will be based on several factors including, but not limited to: knowledge and skills, education, and experience level

• Comprehensive benefits package including paid time off, medical/dental/vision coverage, life insurance, paid parental leave, and many other perks

If you don’t meet 100% of the preferred skills and experience, we encourage you to still apply! Building a spacecraft unlike any other requires a team unlike any other and non-traditional career twists and turns are encouraged!

If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

Export Compliance

As defined in the ITAR, “U.S. Persons” include U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents (i.e., Green Card holders), and certain protected individuals (e.g., refugees/asylees, American Samoans). Please consult with a knowledgeable advisor if you are unsure whether you are a “U.S. Person.”

jobs.title: Government Affairs Intern
jobs.description:
About Us

At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space.



The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy.




ABOUT THE SUMMER INTERNSHIP PROGRAM

Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater.

Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else.

We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer.

 

We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules:

Cohort #1

Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13

Cohort #2

Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10

 

All internship roles are based at one of our offices (Torrance/Idaho Falls/Washington D.C.) and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements.

Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package if eligible.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Antares Nuclear is seeking a highly motivated and resourceful Government Affairs Intern to support the company's government affairs, communications, international business development, and commercial business development efforts from our Washington, D.C. office.

This position offers a unique opportunity to work on emerging national security and energy policy issues while helping advance the commercialization and international deployment of next-generation nuclear technology. The intern will support research, stakeholder engagement, strategic planning, and business development initiatives, working closely with Antares leadership and cross-functional teams.

The ideal candidate is an excellent writer and researcher, has a strong interest in national security, energy, public policy, or emerging technologies, and thrives in a fast-paced environment where initiative and attention to detail are essential.




ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Monitor congressional activity, federal legislation, appropriations, defense authorization, and executive branch initiatives relevant to advanced nuclear energy and microreactor deployment.

 - Research and analyze policy developments across the Pentagon, Department of Energy, Department of State, Department of Commerce, NASA, and other relevant federal agencies.

 - Assist in preparing briefing materials, talking points, policy memoranda, presentations, and other materials for meetings with government officials and congressional offices.

 - Track engagement with congressional offices, federal agencies, military services, and other key stakeholders.

 - Identify opportunities to advance policies, programs, and funding initiatives that support microreactor deployment for national security and commercial applications.

 - Support the development of strategic communications materials that articulate Antares’ mission, technology, and value proposition to government, commercial, and international audiences.

 - Draft and edit executive talking points, briefing materials, presentation content, website copy, and other communications products.

 - Monitor media coverage, industry developments, and public discourse related to advanced nuclear energy, national security, and microreactor deployment.

 - Help translate complex technical and policy issues into clear, accessible messages tailored to different audiences, including policymakers, prospective customers, strategic partners, and the general public.

 - Assist in developing communications strategies for key company milestones, government announcements, industry events, and strategic partnerships.

 - Identify opportunities to raise awareness of Antares’ work through relevant publications, industry forums, conferences, and other external channels.

 - Research international markets and identify countries, government agencies, utilities, defense organizations, and other prospective customers for Antares microreactors.

 - Assess country-level opportunities based on energy demand, national security priorities, regulatory frameworks, financing mechanisms, and government support for nuclear energy.

 - Support engagement with U.S. embassies, the State Department, the Foreign Commercial Service, international partners, and prospective overseas customers.

 - Research foreign government procurement processes, export requirements, financing options, and other factors affecting international reactor deployment.

 - Prepare country profiles, market assessments, customer briefings, and presentations to support Antares' international growth strategy.

 - Identify prospective commercial customers and strategic partners across sectors such as data centers, critical infrastructure, industrial facilities, remote power systems, and other energy-intensive applications.

 - Research customer power requirements, market dynamics, competing energy technologies, and potential use cases for microreactors.

 - Assist with developing customer presentations, market analyses, business cases, and strategic partnership proposals.

 - Maintain and update business development pipelines, stakeholder databases, and opportunity trackers.

 - Support preparation for customer meetings, industry conferences, and strategic partner engagements.




BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in public policy, international relations, political science, economics, business, engineering, energy policy, or a related field.

 - Strong research, analytical, and written communication skills.

 - Demonstrated interest in national security, energy, emerging technologies, international affairs, or commercial strategy.

 - Ability to synthesize complex information into clear, concise briefings and recommendations.

 - Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.

 - Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly PowerPoint, Word, and Excel.

 - A proactive, intellectually curious approach and willingness to take ownership of assignments.




PREFERRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE:

 - Sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to manage sensitive matters and competing priorities in a fast-moving environment.

 - Experience with congressional offices, federal agencies, think tanks, political campaigns, consulting, or business development.

 - Familiarity with U.S. national security policy, federal appropriations, international trade, or the energy sector.

 - Experience conducting market research, developing presentations, or preparing policy and business memoranda.

 - Foreign language proficiency or international experience.




ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

 - Ability to travel as needed for government, regulator, supplier, customer, and international partner engagements.

 - Ability to support time-sensitive milestones or incidents outside standard business hours when necessary.




LOCATION

 - We are located in downtown Washington, DC in a space designed for team collaboration and easy access to Capitol Hill, federal government offices, foreign embassies, and DC-based think tanks.



Culture

At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful:

 - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system

 - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle

 - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done”

 - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together

 - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption
   
   

Equal Opportunity

Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.




ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987.

jobs.title: Sales Manager, Mid-Market - EMEA
jobs.description:
WHY JOIN SALES AT ASHBY

Sales at Ashby is a unique opportunity to sell a product customers genuinely love https://www.ashbyhq.com/customers during an AI-fueled market expansion. Over 5,000 companies rely on Ashby, including OpenAI, Doctolib, Bolt, Mistral and Monday.com http://Monday.com, and our business is durably growing faster than 100% year-over-year. We’re well funded https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/series-d, and on a path to profitability. That's exceptionally rare for a company at our scale, and puts us in the top 10% of benchmarks.

Nearly 1 in 3 of Ashby’s globally distributed team call Europe home! We’ve landed over 1000 customers in EMEA representing ~24% of our global revenue base, spread across UKI, DACH, France & the rest of the region. Clear evidence of strong product-market fit. We’re doubling down our investment in the region with in-market GTM, CS and Support resources. EU Data Residency and product localisation are committed and coming soon. We believe there is a meaningful opportunity to help modern teams move beyond legacy recruiting software.

Ashby replaces 3-5 tools in a consolidation & efficiency play that’s equally loved by recruiters and CFOs. We’re known as a clear AI-leader https://www.ashbyhq.com/ai in the recruiting space. We are rapidly extending from a best-in-class recruiting product toward a multi-product platform, expanding upmarket, into new industries, and internationally. For sales reps, that means a large market full of legacy tools, and a product portfolio that creates room for both new business and expansion. This is a chance to participate in how a category-defining company wins in its next phase of growth.

We are equally intentional about how we build the business. We have established a remote-first, high-performing sales organization that rewards learning and accountability. We use data to set achievable quotas https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/how-we-think-about-sales-quotas-and-incentives-at-ashby, and reward sustained impact with competitive compensation and meaningful upside. We prioritize coaching and career development, with AEs advancing to Enterprise & Leadership roles in just a few years — 38% of the team who have been here more than a year have been promoted or taken on a new role!

You will work with people who care about craft, customer outcomes, and winning together—without sacrificing the trust, autonomy, and balance required to do your best work over the long term. Don’t just take my word for it, see what the team has to say https://www.repvue.com/companies/Ashby about working here.



[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/4ea5f68e-c33e-4ac9-831a-e732bee4a303/8f9d2fd6-1fd4-49d9-81a2-b66850fd33fd/image.png]
 


ABOUT ASHBY

We’re building the next generation of enterprise software and we’re starting with a suite of products that empower talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers to be a driving force for revenue & efficiency via a holistic, data-centric talent strategy. Some of our recent highlights include:

 - Raised series D last year & growing ARR >100% YoY, both Globally and in EMEA.

 - Over 5,000 amazing global customers including some of the fastest growing EMEA Mid Market logos like Synthesia (UK), Camunda (Germany) & Alan.com http://Alan.com (FR).

 - Rapidly moving up-market with no signs of slowing down.

 - Implemented AI https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/recruiting/ai-assisted-application-review-in-practice throughout the platform - Known for our pace of innovation and advanced analytics

 - We have a clear buyer persona and large target market. Plus, we already have multiple products to sell. Revenue is growing >100% Y/Y and we've only taken the first steps towards a much larger opportunity. In short, it's the perfect time to join! 🚀


ABOUT THIS ROLE

We are seeking an experienced SaaS Sales Manager in EMEA to lead our Mid-Market Sales Team; which serves the 101-1,000 FTE market. There are three primary responsibilities that this sales leader will take on:

 1. Be accountable for the revenue results of the segment. Understand the primary revenue drivers for the segment, focus your team's energy on high-impact activities, and partner with Marketing on pipeline generating initiatives.

 2. Provide consistent coaching to enable all Account Executives to achieve their full potential. Identify themes for improvement with individuals and at the team level. Help reps grow in their sales career.

 3. Make high quality hires in lock step with market demand. In general we believe that smaller, high caliber teams can achieve remarkable results.

In this role, you’ll report to our Head of Sales, EMEA (Jack Hanratty https://www.linkedin.com/in/hanrattyjack/) and have a significant impact in defining our go-to-market strategy. The best part about Mid-Market is the combination of high velocity and high value deals and we're already very good at winning both. If we are even moderately successful relative to our ambition, we'll have an incredible growth story to tell in just a few years.




YOU COULD BE A GREAT FIT IF:

 - 💰 You’ve managed a team of Account Executives delivering multi-million ARR/yr at a growth-stage SaaS company.

 - 🥇 You have a proven track record of hiring and onboarding new Account Executives who quickly become top performers. You challenge and support them to continue to grow their careers.

 - 🌎 You have experience managing sales teams in the DACH, French and/or across EMEA markets.

 - 👩‍🏫 You’re a teacher and a coach who loves helping reps hone their craft. You can quickly identify skill or knowledge gaps and deliver coaching that is empathetic and drives tangible improvement.

 - 📊 You have a strong mental model for what sales excellence looks like. At the same time, you're a lifelong learner and are open to new ideas and experimentation.

 - 🤝 You are comfortable jumping into deals to establish executive relationships with customers. You do so without ‘boxing out’ your team.

 - ⚙️ You have an operational mindset and have identified bottlenecks and implemented solutions to accelerate deal flow. You love working with Revenue Ops to continually refine processes and tools.

 - 🤓 You become a product and industry expert. You connect the dots quickly. Customers and your team trust you to provide practical advice and relevant stories.


BONUS

 - You were a high performing Enterprise AE and have upmarket deal strategy experience

 - You have sold complex platform applications to Talent and/or People leaders

 - You are fluent in German and/or French


YOU SHOULDN'T APPLY IF:

 - You're a dashboard-and-forecast manager who doesn't like to get into the deals and daily operations

 - You're not keen on learning about our substantial product. "That's for SEs" isn't how we approach things here.

 - Your sole experience is in the UKI market.


OUR PHILOSOPHY

Here are a few key points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

 - We're highly collaborative and we believe in a team-based sales motion to maximize our win rates on high impact deals

 - We believe in developing subject matter expertise (not just on our product but also the TA space broadly) which allows us to provide a differentiated buyer experience

 - We continue to make material investments in engineering and product because we know at the end of the day, having the best product makes winning new customers easier

We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over decades of experience, and thoughtful & clear communication both internally and with customers.




INTERVIEW PROCESS

Our interview process is designed so you can showcase your achievements and points of learning and apply those in a practical exercise. We'll provide you with some Ashby-specific data so you can develop a well informed perspective on our business and solutions engineering involvement. You’ll have opportunities to ask questions of our team throughout.

The interview process for this role is four rounds in the following order:

 1. Intro Call (30 min) - You'll meet with Recruiting to discuss your fit for the role and address questions about our market and solution

 2. Experience Deep Dive (1 hr) - You'll walk Jack (Head of Sales, EMEA) through your career journey in some detail to highlight your experience, achievements, and points of learning to understand how you've developed into the leader you are today

 3. Presentation (1 hr) - We’ll give you some Ashby data, and have you present a perspective on our business and your approach to sales leadership.

 4. Final Round (2 hrs) - You'll have a set of four interviews with cross-functional interviewers




BENEFITS

 - A product that our prospects & customers are truly excited about https://www.ashbyhq.com/customers

 - Competitive salary, commission and equity.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - Extended health benefits for you and your dependents (subject to availability with our Employer of Record)

Reaching out to hiring managers or recruiters directly won't improve your odds of success. Please focus your energy on the quality of your application.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
The Alzheimer’s Disease Data Initiative is a coalition of leading academic, advocacy, government, industry, and philanthropy organizations that recognizes the need for dementia researchers to find easier ways to share unpublished data, analytical tools, and scientific findings. These partners are working together to accelerate progress towards new diagnostics, treatments, and cures in Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD).

In 2020, the AD Data Initiative publicly launched a non-profit organization to implement the mission of the AD Data Initiative coalition and lead us to a future where open data and global collaboration power the end of ADRD.

The AD Data Initiative removes silos by unlocking important ADRD datasets, enabling seamless access to interoperable data sharing platforms, empowering researchers and fostering collaboration to accelerate new breakthroughs.

POSITION OVERVIEW

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the Alzheimer's Disease Workbench (AD Workbench), our secure, cloud-based data platform for ADRD research. You'll be accountable for AD Workbench end to end setting the roadmap, staying close to the researchers and partners who use it, keeping the platform healthy and cost-sustainable, and working closely with the Product & Engineering org to deliver what users need next.

This role sits at the intersection of user’s satisfaction, operations, and product. You'll know AD Workbench users deeply, bring clarity to fuzzy requirements, and carry the voice of the user into every product decision. You'll serve as the day-to-day owner of the AD Workbench partner relationship and oversee platform support delivered by our application management services (AMS) team. You won't work tickets yourself; instead, you'll bring the context behind each request and the judgment to confirm the team is focused on what matters most to users.

The right person is comfortable operating in a startup environment, pairs a strong customer focus with meticulous attention to detail, and treats cost as a product requirement. Clear, concise written and verbal communication with both executive and engineering stakeholders is critical to success, as is the habit of tracking and following up without being asked. A growth mindset, strong accountability, and the ability to learn quickly while consistently delivering results are essential.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

What you'll own

• Own the AD Workbench product roadmap end to end, leading quarterly and monthly goal setting and sign-off, and balancing near-term user needs against long-term platform scalability and clinical validity.

• Translate researcher and partner needs into a prioritized backlog, and make the call on trade-offs when engineering capacity, data governance requirements, and customer timelines pull in different directions.

• Drive high Net Satisfaction among existing and new users and partners and track it alongside adoption and platform health to guide iteration.

Users & partners

• Know AD Workbench users deeply: surface their pain points, bring clarity to fuzzy requirements, and act to close the gap between what the platform does today and what users need it to do.

• Field user questions and issues promptly, resolve what you can, and escalate early and clearly when you can't.

• Bring the voice of the user into product decisions, from backlog prioritization to roadmap reviews.

• Serve as the day-to-day owner of the AD Workbench partner relationship.

Platform support & costs

• Own the day-to-day health of AD Workbench support: review the incoming queue daily, understand what is breaking and why, and make sure nothing sits unattended.

• Partner with the AMS team that handles day-to-day support, bringing the context behind each request and confirming the team is prioritizing what matters most to users.

• Understand what AD Workbench costs to run and what drives those costs; keep spending within budget, monitor for unexpected spikes, and raise them promptly rather than letting them compound.

Internal coordination

• Keep leadership current on platform health, risks, and upcoming decisions, clearly and concisely, without needing to be asked.

• Act as the primary point of contact for internal communications on AD Workbench, tracking open items and following up through to resolution.

• Work closely with engineering to keep AD Workbench stable as the product evolves, providing additional detail and context on requirements when needed.

REQUIRED SKILLS

• 5+ years of product management experience, including ownership of a data, cloud, or SaaS platform used by technical or research audiences.

• Demonstrated experience owning a product roadmap end to end, from user and partner discovery through prioritization, delivery, and iteration, and making clear trade-off decisions under competing constraints.

• Strong customer and partner orientation: able to turn ambiguous feedback into clear problem statements and requirements, and to manage partner relationships day to day.

• Experience overseeing production support or operations, ideally through a managed service (AMS) or vendor team: triaging issues, setting priorities, and holding teams to service levels.

• Cloud cost fluency: understanding what drives platform spend, monitoring it against budget, and acting quickly on anomalies.

• Sufficient technical fluency to work credibly with engineering on cloud platforms (Azure preferred), data access and security controls, and API/service design.

• Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to brief executives clearly and concisely and to give engineering the detail and context it needs.

• Strong organizational discipline: tracking commitments, following up, and closing loops across multiple stakeholders.

• Bonus: experience in a regulated, research, healthcare, or scientific-data domain, where privacy, data governance, and partner trust are first-order product constraints.

QUALIFICATIONS OR RELATED EXPERIENCE

• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, data science, bioinformatics, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. An advanced degree is a plus.

• Experience managing or supporting research data platforms, such as secure data environments, trusted research environments (TREs), data commons, or federated analysis systems.

• Experience working with managed service providers or vendor engineering teams, including SLA-based support models and ticketing tools (e.g., ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, Zendesk).

• Experience with cloud cost management and FinOps practices, such as Azure Cost Management, budgeting, and spend alerting.

• Experience measuring user satisfaction (e.g., Net Satisfaction, NPS, CSAT) and using it to drive product decisions.

• Experience with Agile delivery and product tooling, such as Azure DevOps, Jira, and product analytics or user-feedback tools.

Bonus:

• Experience working in mission-driven organizations or with high-profile stakeholders.

• Experience in life sciences, ideally neuroscience or Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD).

COMPENSATION/TERMS

This is a contracted role. The salary range for this position is $200,000 to $210,000 per year. Offers will vary depending on several factors, including education, experience, and qualifications.

jobs.title: Externship Coordinator – 3+ Years Medical Assisting Experience Required
jobs.description:
The Medical Assisting Externship Coordinator plays a vital role in supporting student transitions from classroom instruction to hands-on training at externship sites, with a focus on employment outcomes. This position is responsible for managing all aspects of the externship experience, from site development and student placement to compliance, documentation, and post-externship employment conversions. While prior experience as a Medical Assistant is not required, successful candidates will demonstrate strong project management, relationship-building, and follow-through skills, preferably with experience in healthcare, workforce development, or community outreach. A key performance benchmark is converting at least 50% of externship placements into job offers, with a goal of 70%.

• Secure, maintain, and expand a network of externship sites with a focus on employers seeking to hire students post-externship.
• Coordinate timely student placements to ensure the externship begins concurrently with the start of the externship module.
• Monitor student attendance and completion of externship hours; track progress to ensure timely graduation.
• Conduct site visits, mid-point, and final evaluations to assess the quality of the learning environment and student performance.
• Ensure all required immunizations and documentation are completed prior to site placement.
• Collaborate with Career Services to align externship opportunities with potential employment outcomes.
• Maintain detailed records and documentation in accordance with programmatic, accreditation, and regulatory requirements.
• Educate and support site supervisors and students on externship policies, expectations, and procedures.
• Provide exceptional student service through regular communication, troubleshooting concerns, and supporting retention and program completion.
• Represent the program professionally with community partners and employers; participate in career fairs or other outreach events as needed.

Hours are generally, one late shift per week, until 7:00pm – 8:00pm, will be needed to ensure quality support and availability to evening students.

Pay Range: $31-$35/hr (Actual starting base pay may vary based on factors such as education, experience, skills, location, and budget.)

• Active Medical Assistant license with proven 3 years experience.
• Associate’s degree or higher preferred; equivalent work experience in community outreach, workforce development, healthcare partnerships or as a Medical Assistant will be considered.
• 3 years of experience as a Medical Assistant, proficient in both front- and back-office operations.
• 2 years of experience in project coordination, community engagement, and employer relations, with additional background in sales/marketing; career services experience strongly preferred.
• Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
• Excellent communication, interpersonal, and customer service skills.
• Knowledge of or experience in the healthcare industry is a plus.
• Must have a valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, and the ability to travel regularly for site visits.
• Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and comfortable working within a data tracking system, Student Information System or CRM.
• Familiarity with accreditation standards, externship program coordination, or student services preferred.

We Offer:

• Medical, Dental and Vision starting the 1st of the month following 30 days of employment
• 2 Weeks’ starting Vacation per year. Increasing based on years of service with company
• 12 paid Holidays and 2 Floating Holiday
• 401K with a Company Match
• Company Paid Life Insurance at 1x’s your annual salary
• Leadership development and training for career advancement
• Tuition assistance and Forgiveness for you and your family up to 100% depending on program

jobs.title: Mission Engineer II - Grand Rapids
jobs.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

This isn't a relationship management role. It's an ownership role. Sharp. Adaptable. Unstoppable. As a Mission Engineer II, you'll work directly alongside public safety agencies to turn real operational challenges into working technical solutions.

You'll spend time with the people doing the work, understand how the agency operates, identify problems worth solving, and use Axon tools, AI, automation, data, and the broader Axon ecosystem to build against them.

Building is the core of the role, but customer needs come first. Because you're embedded with the agency, you'll also become a go-to technical resource who understands their Axon environment and helps them navigate critical needs when they arise. You may help quarterback an upcoming deployment, coordinate a complex technical issue, or connect the right Axon teams around an agency priority.

You won't replace Support, Deployment, Product, or other teams. You'll bring technical continuity, help connect the dots, and use what you learn to identify the next opportunity to build something better. Mission Engineers don't measure success by activity. They measure it by what gets built, what gets used, and what changes because of it.

What You’ll Do

Location: On Site with travel
Reports To: Manager or Senior Manager of Mission Engineering

Discover the Mission

• Embed with assigned agencies to understand their mission, people, workflows, systems, and priorities.

• Develop broad knowledge of the Axon ecosystem and deeper expertise in the products deployed at your agency.

• Work with frontline users, technical teams, and agency leadership to uncover operational friction.

• Translate customer problems into clear technical requirements and measurable success criteria.

• Identify opportunities for AI, automation, data, and Axon capabilities to improve how the agency operates.

• Understand what the customer needs—not simply what they initially ask for.

Build With the Platform

• Build applications, dashboards, workflows, automations, and using Axon products and other approved Axon tools.

• Apply foundational software engineering concepts including APIs, data structures, scripting, testing, debugging, and version control.

• Use AI and AI-assisted development tools responsibly within Axon's approved development and security environment.

• Configure and extend capabilities across Axon's technology ecosystem.

• Understand when you can solve the problem yourself and when deeper Product or Engineering partnership is required.

• Build with Axon—not around it.

Transform Builds Into Outcomes

• Move solutions from discovery into real customer use.

• Test and iterate alongside the people who will actually use what you build.

• Drive adoption and measure results against agreed success criteria.

• Continue improving solutions until they create sustained operational value.

• Document successful solutions so they can be maintained, improved, and reused.

Be the Agency's Go-To Technical Resource

• Maintain a consistent onsite presence and deep understanding of the agency's Axon environment.

• Lean into critical customer needs when your technical context or involvement can materially improve the outcome.

• Help quarterback technical alignment around important deployments without replacing the teams responsible for deployment execution.

• Serve as a liaison when complex technical issues require coordination beyond standard Support.

• Help customers navigate capabilities across products such as Records, Fusus, AI Era, and the broader Axon ecosystem.

• Connect the right resources across Product, Engineering, Support, Deployment, Training, Mission Operations, Mission Success, and Sales.

• Continuously ask: What are we learning, what could work better, and what could we build so this is easier next time?

• Return to the highest-value build opportunities once immediate customer needs are addressed.

Learn in the Field. Improve Axon.

• Capture recurring customer needs, workflow patterns, and technical friction.

• Share successful builds and lessons across Mission Engineering.

• Bring platform limitations and customer insights back to Product and Engineering.

• Identify solutions that could be reused by other MEs and agencies.

What You Bring

Required

• Typically 3–5+ years of experience in solutions engineering, software engineering, systems, technical consulting, implementation engineering, or another hands-on technical role.

• Foundational software engineering capability and demonstrated experience building technical solutions.

• Working knowledge of APIs, scripting/ programming, data, testing, debugging, and modern development practices.

• Understanding of AI concepts and practical applications.

• Strong technical curiosity and ability to rapidly learn emerging platforms and tools.

• Ability to solve ambiguous problems rather than simply execute predefined tasks.

• Strong communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences.

• Customer-facing mindset and curiosity about how organizations actually operate.

• Ability to obtain and maintain CJIS compliance and satisfy applicable agency background requirements.

• Ability to maintain the onsite presence required by the engagement.

Preferred

• Experience with Python, JavaScript, SQL, REST APIs, cloud platforms, or modern frameworks.

• Experience with AI platforms, workflow automation, low-code development, or data.

• Experience in public safety, defense, military, intelligence, government, or other mission-critical environments.

What Success Looks Like

You can take a meaningful customer problem through:

Discover → Build → Transform

Given Axon's approved toolkit, and a problem worth solving, you can turn it into a working solution and demonstrate whether it created value. And when the agency needs you elsewhere, you lean in without losing the engineering mindset—help solve the immediate need, identify what can be improved, and return to building.

Benefits that Benefit You

• Competitive salary and 401k with employer match

• Discretionary paid time off

• Paid parental leave for all

• Medical, Dental, Vision plans

• Fitness Programs

• Emotional & Mental Wellness support

• Learning & Development programs

Benefits listed herein may vary depending on the nature of your employment and the location where you work

Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Important Notes

The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. The job description may change or be supplemented at any time in accordance with business needs and conditions.

Some roles may also require legal eligibility to work in a firearms environment.

We collect personal information from applicants to evaluate candidates for employment. You may request access, deletion, or exercise other CCPA rights at axongreenhousesupport@axon.com or via our Axon Privacy Web Form. For more information, please see the Your California Privacy Rights section of our Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice.

Axon’s mission is to Protect Life and is committed to the well-being and safety of its employees as well as Axon’s impact on the environment. All Axon employees must be aware of and committed to the appropriate environmental, health, and safety regulations, policies, and procedures. Axon employees are empowered to report safety concerns as they arise and activities potentially impacting the environment.

We are an equal opportunity employer that promotes justice, advances equity, values diversity and fosters inclusion. We’re committed to hiring the best talent — regardless of race, creed, color, ancestry, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances — and empowering all of our employees so they can do their best work. If you have a disability or special need that requires assistance or accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please email recruitingops@axon.com.  Please note that this email address is for accommodation purposes only. Axon will not respond to inquiries for other purposes.

Phishing alert:  Axon will never ask you to pay for any part of the hiring process, including training, equipment, or background checks. We do not make job offers via text message, WhatsApp, or instant messaging platforms without a formal interview process.  All legitimate job openings are listed on our official careers page at https://www.axon.com/careers.  If you receive a suspicious offer or outreach from an email address that is not @axon.com, or if you are asked for sensitive personal information (bank details, Social Security Number) prematurely, please ignore the message and report it to recruitingops@axon.com.
